ITQAN:v2p566/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p566/r12.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p566/r12.claim: فرادى is a plural form of أفراد, itself the plural of فرد.

TABATABAI:14:19-34#8/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:19-34#8/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:19-34#8/r4.claim: “Neither can you rescue me” implies the bond between Iblis and followers has ended; otherwise it would be needless. Their earthly following provides no tie or aid now.
TABATABAI:14:19-34#8/r4.anchor: وظاهر السياق أن قوله { ما أنا بمصرخكم وما أنتم بمصرخي } كناية عن انتفاء الرابطة بينه وبين تابعيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p560/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p560/r7.speaker: أبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p560/r7.claim: Abu al-Baqa treats the declined form فرادا as a rare plural like تؤام and رخال; other analyses derive it from فَرْد or فريد.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p560/r7.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: من صرفه جعله جمعا مثل تؤام ورخال وهو جمع قليل، قيل: وفرادى جمع فرد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p560/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p560/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p560/r8.claim: خوله means he gave, granted, and made someone owner of something.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p560/r8.anchor: خوله: أعطاه وملكه وأصله تمليك الخول كما تقول مولته ملكته المال.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p560/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p560/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p560/r9.claim: البين usually means separation but may also mean connection; a line of poetry illustrates the shared form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p560/r9.anchor: البين: الفراق. قيل: وينطلق على الوصل فيكون مشتركا. قال الشاعر:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya analyzes the verb as having an omitted subject meaning the connection between the idolaters and their alleged partners broke; Mujahid and al-Suddi are said to explain it this way.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r1.anchor: لقد تقطع الاتصال والارتباط بينكم أو نحو هذا وهذا وجه واضح وعليه فسره الناس مجاهد والسدي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r2.claim: The omitted-subject analysis fails because an Arabic sentence cannot simply omit its subject.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r2.anchor: وقوله إلى شيء محذوف ليس بصحيح لأن الفاعل لا يحذف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqaʾ proposes an omitted subject qualified by baynakum, or by a word meaning connection, but the author rejects deletion of the subject.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r3.anchor: أن يكون بينكم صفة لفاعل محذوف أي لقد تقطع شيء بينكم أو وصل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r4.claim: He prefers an instance of syntactic competition: ḍalla governs the shared object, while taqaṭṭaʿa has an implicit pronoun referring to the idols.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r4.anchor: أن المسألة من باب الإعمال تسلط على ما كنتم تزعمون تقطع وضل فأعمل الثاني

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r5.claim: The sense is that the claimed partnership has broken apart and the supposed partners have vanished, as in the verse about ties being severed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r5.anchor: لم يبق اتصال بينكم وبين ما كنتم تزعمون أنهم شركاء فعبدتموهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r6.speaker: عبد الله ومجاهد والأعمش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r6.claim: They read mā baynakum, meaning the bond between you and your alleged partners has perished.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r6.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله ومجاهد والأعمش ما بينكم والمعنى تلف وذهب ما بينكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r7.claim: The two objects of taẓʿamūn are omitted but understood as the idols and their intercessory status; the cited verse illustrates such ellipsis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r7.anchor: ومفعولا تزعمون محذوفان التقدير تزعمونهم شفعاء حذفا للدلالة عليهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r8.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r8.claim: Al-Razi reads the verse as the severing of the connection between soul and body, but Abu Hayyan says this meaning is not expressed by the verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p588/r8.anchor: المعنى أن الوصلة الحاصلة بين النفس والجسد قد انقطعت ولا سبيل إلى تحصيلها

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p412/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p412/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p412/r3.claim: Ashtāt means separately or singly: people emerge without family, tribe, companions, wealth, supporters, or intercessors, as also stated in 19:95 and 6:94.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p412/r3.anchor: means “in a separate or solitary manner.” In other words

IBNMUJAHID:v1p262/r6.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p262/r6.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم برواية أبي بكر وابن عامر وحمزة
IBNMUJAHID:v1p262/r6.claim: They raise the nūn in لقد تقطع بينكم; Nafi and al-Kisai, plus Hafs from Asim, read it accusative.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p262/r6.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم فى رواية أبى بكر وابن عامر وحمزة ﴿ لقد تقطع بينكم ﴾ رفعا

MAJAZ:v1p200/r8.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p200/r8.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p200/r8.claim: Furādā means individually, one by one.

MAJAZ:v1p200/r9.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p200/r9.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p200/r9.claim: Taqaṭṭaʿ baynakum means your bond has been severed; the construction is nominative because the verb governs it.
MAJAZ:v1p200/r9.anchor: «تقطع بينكم» (94) [أي وصلكم] مرفوع لأن الفعل عمل فيه،

MAJAZ:v1p200/r10.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p200/r10.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p200/r10.claim: Muhalhil’s verse provides an example of bayna in the same grammatical construction.
MAJAZ:v1p200/r10.anchor:
كما قال مهلهل:
كأن رماحهم أشطان بئر ... بعيد بين جاليها جرور

STUDYQURAN:6:94/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:94/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:94/r1.claim: Though the Resurrection is a universal judgment, every person experiences utter aloneness.
STUDYQURAN:6:94/r1.anchor: although the Day of Resurrection is a day of universal judgment, every person will feel utterly alone

STUDYQURAN:6:94/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:94/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:94/r2.claim: People return alone as they were first created, and naked, wholly dependent on God.

STUDYQURAN:6:94/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:94/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:94/r3.claim: Judgment comes without worldly means, wealth, associates, or children that had provided status and protection; these goods are left behind.
STUDYQURAN:6:94/r3.anchor: without the benefit of their worldly means, wealth, associates, and children (Z)

STUDYQURAN:6:94/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:94/r4.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:6:94/r4.claim: Worldly goods and the bond to them are left behind, but knowledge of God, virtue, and good deeds are sent ahead and met with greater reward.
STUDYQURAN:6:94/r4.anchor: Al-Rāzī explains that, although worldly goods are left behind and that the connection between these goods and the one who strove to acquire them is severed

STUDYQURAN:6:94/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:94/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:94/r5.claim: The supposed intercessors are false idols or deities claimed as God's partners and credited with power to intercede.
STUDYQURAN:6:94/r5.anchor: Your intercessors here refers to the false idols or deities they had ascribed as partners unto God

STUDYQURAN:6:94/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:94/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:94/r6.claim: The Quran repeatedly depicts false idols, deities, authorities, and Satan disowning or forsaking their earthly followers.
STUDYQURAN:6:94/r6.anchor: false idols, deities, and authorities, including Satan, will disown and “forsake” those who followed or venerated them

TAB-FULL:v9p413/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p413/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p413/r1.claim: At resurrection the idolaters come singly, without wealth, possessions, companions, or anything God gave them, just as they were first created, naked and barefoot.
TAB-FULL:v9p413/r1.anchor: ويعني بقوله: (فرادى) : وحدانا، لا مال معهم

TAB-FULL:v9p413/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p413/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p413/r2.claim: They return as when first created: naked, uncircumcised, and barefoot, with nothing they used to boast of in worldly life.
TAB-FULL:v9p413/r2.anchor: عراة غلفا غرلا حفاة كما ولدتهم أمهاتهم، وكما خلقهم جل ثناؤه في بطون أمهاتهم، لا شيء عليهم ولا معهم

TAB-FULL:v9p413/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p413/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p413/r3.claim: Furādā is a plural whose singular is fard; related forms include fard and farīd, just as waḥd, waḥad, and waḥīd are forms for one.
TAB-FULL:v9p413/r3.anchor: وفرادى جمع، يقال لواحدها: فرد، كما قال نابغة بني ذبيان

TAB-FULL:v9p413/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p413/r4.speaker: النابغة الذبياني
TAB-FULL:v9p413/r4.claim: Al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī uses al-fard in a line comparing an animal to a polished, solitary sword.
TAB-FULL:v9p413/r4.anchor: من وحش وجرة موشي أكارعه … طاوي المصير كسيف الصيقل الفرد

TAB-FULL:v9p413/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p413/r5.speaker: شاعر
TAB-FULL:v9p413/r5.claim: An unnamed poet uses furād alongside “in pairs,” illustrating its plural sense.
TAB-FULL:v9p413/r5.anchor: ترى النعرات الزرق فوق لبانه … فراد ومثنى أصعقتها صواهله

TAB-FULL:v9p413/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p413/r6.speaker: يونس الجرمي
TAB-FULL:v9p413/r6.claim: Yūnus al-Jarmī says furād is the plural of fard, like tuʾam and tuʾām for twins; he also cites forms such as al-farādā and al-ridāfā.
TAB-FULL:v9p413/r6.anchor: وكان يونس الجرمي فيما ذكر عنه يقول: فراد جمع فرد، كما قيل: توءم وتؤام للجميع

TAB-FULL:v9p413/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p413/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p413/r7.claim: A man or woman called fard is one without a sibling.
TAB-FULL:v9p413/r7.anchor: ويقال: رجل فرد، وامرأة فرد، إذا لم يكن لها أخ

TAB-FULL:v9p413/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p413/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v9p413/r8.claim: When ʿĀʾisha worried that men and women would be resurrected together and see one another naked, the Prophet said each would be occupied with his or her own affair and not look at the other sex.
TAB-FULL:v9p413/r8.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لكل امرئ منهم يومئذ شأن يغنيه

TAB-FULL:v9p416/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p416/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p416/r1.claim: The people left behind what God enabled them to possess in worldly life and once boasted of; the wording rebukes their pride in wealth.
TAB-FULL:v9p416/r1.anchor: وبنحو الذي قلنا في ذلك قال أهل التأويل

TAB-FULL:v9p416/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p416/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p416/r2.claim: To khawwala is to give or grant something to another person; Ṭabarī cites usage from poetry.
TAB-FULL:v9p416/r2.anchor: ما ملكته غيرك وأعطيته فقد خولته

TAB-FULL:v9p416/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p416/r3.speaker: أبو النجم
TAB-FULL:v9p416/r3.claim: Abū al-Najm’s line uses khawwala for giving generously and the phrase khawwala al-mukhawwal.
TAB-FULL:v9p416/r3.anchor: ومنه قول أبي النجم: [البحر الرجز] أعطى فلم يبخل ولم يبخل … كوم الذرا من خول المخول

TAB-FULL:v9p416/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p416/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
TAB-FULL:v9p416/r4.claim: Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ recited Zuhayr’s line using yastakhwilū al-māl, supporting the sense of granting wealth.
TAB-FULL:v9p416/r4.anchor: وقد ذكر أن أبا عمرو بن العلاء كان ينشد بيت زهير: [البحر الطويل] هنالك إن يستخولوا المال يخولوا

TAB-FULL:v9p416/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p416/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v9p416/r5.claim: Al-Suddī glosses what God bestowed as wealth and servants that people left behind in worldly life.
TAB-FULL:v9p416/r5.anchor: عن السدي: {وتركتم ما خولناكم} [الأنعام: 94] من المال والخدم {وراء ظهوركم}

TAB-FULL:v9p416#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p416#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p416#2/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains that the supposed intercessors were the idols people claimed would plead for them before God at resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v9p416#2/r1.anchor: عن السدي: أما قوله: {وما نرى معكم شفعاءكم الذين زعمتم أنهم فيكم شركاء} [الأنعام: 94]

TAB-FULL:v9p416#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p416#2/r2.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v9p416#2/r2.claim: One reported occasion links the verse to al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, who said al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā would intercede for him.
TAB-FULL:v9p416#2/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة، قال: " قال النضر بن الحارث: سوف تشفع لي اللات والعزى، فنزلت هذه الآية

TAB-FULL:v9p416#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p416#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v9p416#2/r3.claim: Another view says the passage concerns the general claim of all idol worshippers that their gods were intercessors.
TAB-FULL:v9p416#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: إن ذلك كان قول كافة عبدة الأوثان

TAB-FULL:v9p416#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p416#2/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v9p416#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddī says the polytheists worshipped idols on the claim that they would intercede with God and that they were His partners.
TAB-FULL:v9p416#2/r4.anchor: عن السدي: أما قوله: {وما نرى معكم شفعاءكم الذين زعمتم أنهم فيكم شركاء} [الأنعام: 94] ، «فإن المشركين كانوا يزعمون

TAB-FULL:v9p417/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p417/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p417/r1.claim: On Judgment Day the worldly ties, affection, and mutual support among the idolaters vanish; none contacts or aids another.
TAB-FULL:v9p417/r1.anchor: فاضمحل ذلك كله في الآخرة، فلا أحد منهم ينصر صاحبه ولا يواصله

TAB-FULL:v9p417/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p417/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v9p417/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses the severed bond as the idolaters’ worldly mutual contact.
TAB-FULL:v9p417/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد: {لقد تقطع بينكم} [الأنعام: 94] البين: تواصلهم

TAB-FULL:v9p417/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p417/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v9p417/r3.claim: Qatada explains the severed bond as the connection and ties that existed among them.
TAB-FULL:v9p417/r3.anchor: عن معمر، عن قتادة: {لقد تقطع بينكم} [الأنعام: 94] قال: «وصلكم»

TAB-FULL:v9p417/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p417/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v9p417/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets what is severed and lost as kinship ties and homes.
TAB-FULL:v9p417/r4.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: {لقد تقطع بينكم وضل عنكم ما كنتم تزعمون} [الأنعام: 94] يعني: «الأرحام والمنازل»

TAB-FULL:v9p417/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p417/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v9p417/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says that what was between them is cut off.
TAB-FULL:v9p417/r5.anchor: عن السدي: {لقد تقطع بينكم} [الأنعام: 94] يقول: «تقطع ما بينكم»

TAB-FULL:v9p417/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p417/r6.speaker: أبو بكر بن عياش
TAB-FULL:v9p417/r6.claim: Abu Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh glosses the phrase as their worldly mutual contact.
TAB-FULL:v9p417/r6.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن عياش: {لقد تقطع بينكم} [الأنعام: 94] «التواصل في الدنيا»

TAB-FULL:v9p417/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p417/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p417/r7.claim: Most Medinan readers recite بينكم in the accusative, meaning what is between you; most Meccan and Iraqi readers recite it nominatively, meaning your bond.
TAB-FULL:v9p417/r7.anchor: فقرأته عامة قراء أهل المدينة نصبا بمعنى: لقد تقطع ما بينكم

TAB-FULL:v9p417/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p417/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p417/r8.claim: Both well-known readings are sound and agree in meaning; either reading is correct because Arabic attests both accusative بين as a noun and nominative use when it functions as one.
TAB-FULL:v9p417/r8.anchor: والصواب من القول عندي في ذلك أن يقال: إنهما قراءتان مشهورتان

TAB-FULL:v9p417/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p417/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p417/r9.claim: Arabic attests accusative بين in a noun position and also nominative بين when it functions as a noun.
TAB-FULL:v9p417/r9.anchor: وقد ذكر عنها سماعا الرفع في (بين) إذا كان الفعل لها وجعلت اسما

TAB-FULL:v9p419/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p419/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p419/r1.claim: The hemistich of مهلهل uses raised بين because it functions as a noun; accusative use is more common whether بين is adjectival or nominal.
TAB-FULL:v9p419/r1.anchor: كأن رماحهم أشطان بئر … بعيد بين جاليها جرور

TABATABAI:6:93-94/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:93-94/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:93-94/r4.claim: Farādā means individuals detached from others, contrasted with a pair and conceptually close to odd versus even.
TABATABAI:6:93-94/r4.anchor: الفرادى جمع فرد وهو الذي انفصل عن اختلاط غيره نوعا من الاختلاط

TABATABAI:6:93-94/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:93-94/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:93-94/r5.claim: Takhwīl means giving assets or similar resources that a person manages and disposes of.
TABATABAI:6:93-94/r5.anchor: والتخويل إعطاء الخول أي المال ونحوه الذي يقوم الإنسان به بالتدبير والتصرف

TABATABAI:6:93-94/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:93-94/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:93-94/r6.claim: The alleged intercessors are deities worshipped apart from God to intercede with Him, thereby treated as partners in His creation.
TABATABAI:6:93-94/r6.anchor: والمراد بالشفعاء الأرباب المعبودون من دون الله ليكونوا شفعاء عند الله فعادوا بذلك شركاء لله سبحانه في خلقه

TABATABAI:6:93-94/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:93-94/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:93-94/r7.claim: At return to God after death, people appear alone as at their first creation and recognize that God alone governed them; wealth, family, social backing, and alleged intercessors were false claims without real creative power.
TABATABAI:6:93-94/r7.anchor: والآية تنبئ عن حقيقة الحياة الإنسانية التي ستظهر له حينما يقدم على ربه بالتوفي فيشاهد حقيقة أمر نفسه

TABATABAI:6:93-94/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:93-94/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:93-94/r8.claim: Human beings and all other things remain under God's governance and goal; apparent causes are only means whose effects end in God and possess no independent efficacy, though worldly desire makes people treat them as autonomous.
TABATABAI:6:93-94/r8.anchor: فالإنسان جزء من أجزاء الكون واقع تحت التدبير الإلهي متوجه إلى الغاية التي غياها الله سبحانه له كسائر أجزاء الكون

TABATABAI:6:94-96/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r1.claim: Worldly life distracts people from servitude; forgetting God leads them to forget themselves, while death exposes their dependence on Him.
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r1.anchor: الإنسان إذا خرج عن زي العبودية نسي ربه فأداه ذلك إلى نسيان نفسه

TABATABAI:6:94-96/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r2.claim: At death, bodily separation severs a person from material causes and reveals that only God governs his affairs.
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r2.anchor: إذا فارقت نفسه البدن بحلول الموت بطل ارتباطه بجميع الأسباب والعلل والمعدات المادية

TABATABAI:6:94-96/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r3.claim: Arriving alone before God, as at first creation, states the underlying reality of the human condition.
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r3.anchor: فقوله تعالى { ولقد جئتمونا فرادى كما خلقناكم أول مرة } إشارة إلى حقيقة الأمر

TABATABAI:6:94-96/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r4.claim: Leaving bestowed possessions behind shows that the distracting causes between first creation and return to God are invalid as independent supports.
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r4.anchor: بيان لبطلان الأسباب الملهية له عن ربه المتخللة بين أول خلقه وبين يوم يقبض فيه إلى ربه

TABATABAI:6:94-96/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r5.claim: The imagined associates lose all independence and influence when their falsehood is exposed; they were delusions people played with in worldly life.
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r5.anchor: وان السبب في ذلك انكشاف بطلان المزاعم التي كان الإنسان يلعب بها طول حياته الدنيا

TABATABAI:6:94-96/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r6.claim: Because 6:94 denies independent causes and false divine partners, the next passage explains that those causes are God's managed creations and act only by His measure.
TABATABAI:6:94-96/r6.anchor: لما انتهى الكلام في الآية السابقة إلى نفي استقلال الأسباب في تأثيرها، وبطلان كون أربابهم شفعاء من دون الله

TABATABAI:6:91-105#13/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:91-105#13/r9.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABATABAI:6:91-105#13/r9.claim: A report from al-Sadiq describes Adam’s creation from two handfuls of clay gathered from the heavens and earth: the right-hand portion was destined for prophets, believers, and the honored; the left for tyrants, polytheists, hypocrites, and the wretched.
TABATABAI:6:91-105#13/r9.anchor: عن إبراهيم عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال إن الله عز وجل لما أراد أن يخلق آدم بعث جبرئيل

TABRISI:6:94/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94/r1.speaker: أهل المدينة والكسائي وحفص
TABRISI:6:94/r1.claim: The people of Medina, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ read baynakum in the accusative; the other readers use the nominative.
TABRISI:6:94/r1.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة والكسائي وحفص بينكم بالنصب والباقون بالرفع

TABRISI:6:94/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94/r2.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:6:94/r2.claim: Abu Ali says bayn can be an inflected noun, like iftirāq, or an adverb; the nominative reading treats an originally adverbial form as a noun that can be the subject of taqaṭṭaʿa.
TABRISI:6:94/r2.anchor: قال أبو علي: استعمل هذا الاسم على ضربين

TABRISI:6:94/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94/r3.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:6:94/r3.claim: The nominative cannot mean that your separation was severed; it means your bond was severed, since the intended sense is the connection that united you.
TABRISI:6:94/r3.anchor: لأن المراد لقد تقطع وصلكم وما كنتم تتألفون عليه

TABRISI:6:94/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94/r4.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:6:94/r4.claim: Though bayn originally suggests separation, its use for ties of kinship, friendship, and partnership made it mean connection, so taqaṭṭaʿa baynakum can mean your bond was severed.
TABRISI:6:94/r4.anchor: لما استعمل مع الشيئين المتلابسين في نحو بيني وبينه شركة وبيني وبينه رحم وصداقة صارت لاستعمالها في هذه المواضع بمنزلة الوصلة

TABRISI:6:94/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:94/r5.claim: One analysis of the accusative supplies the omitted subject waṣl, inferred from the preceding denial of intercessors.
TABRISI:6:94/r5.anchor: أنه أضمر الفاعل في الفعل ودل عليه ما تقدم من قوله { وما نرى معكم شفعاءكم }

TABRISI:6:94/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94/r6.speaker: سيبويه
TABRISI:6:94/r6.claim: Sibawayh’s reported usage allows an omitted contextual circumstance, as in their saying, if it is tomorrow, come to me.
TABRISI:6:94/r6.anchor: وقد حكى سيبويه أنهم قالوا إذا كان غدا فأتني وأضمر ما كانوا فيه من رخاء وبلاء

TABRISI:6:94/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94/r7.speaker: أبو الحسن
TABRISI:6:94/r7.claim: Abu al-Hasan treats the accusative as having the nominative reading’s meaning while retaining the usual adverbial form; he compares expressions whose meaning is nominative.
TABRISI:6:94/r7.anchor: أنه انتصب على شيء يراه أبو الحسن فإنه يذهب إلى أن معناه معنى المرفوع

TABRISI:6:94/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:94/r8.claim: Furādā is a plural of fard, farīd, and fard; Arabs also use furādā and furād without declension, by analogy with thulāth and rubāʿ.
TABRISI:6:94/r8.anchor: فرادى جمع فرد وفريد وفرد والعرب تقول فرادى وفراد فلا يصرفونها تشبيها بثلاث ورباع

TABRISI:6:94#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:94#2/r1.claim: The cited poetry uses furād and mathnā for single and paired horses, illustrating the forms.
TABRISI:6:94#2/r1.anchor:
ترى النعرات البيض تحت لبانه
فراد ومثنى أصعقتها صواهله

TABRISI:6:94#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94#2/r2.speaker: النابغة
TABRISI:6:94#2/r2.claim: Al-Nābigha’s phrase al-fard, likening a lean animal to a polished sword, supplies another example of the singular form.
TABRISI:6:94#2/r2.anchor: وقال النابغة: من وحش وجرة موشي أكارعه

TABRISI:6:94#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:94#2/r3.claim: Al-ridāfā and al-qirābā are analogous plural forms to furādā.

TABRISI:6:94#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:94#2/r4.claim: Takhwīl means giving or granting; its root sense is making someone owner of dependents, just as tamwīl makes someone owner of wealth.
TABRISI:6:94#2/r4.anchor: والتخويل الإعطاء وأصله تمليك الخول كما أن التمويل هو تمليك الأموال

TABRISI:6:94#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:94#2/r5.claim: Khawwala means God gave someone wealth; khawli māl, khāl māl, and khāʾil māl describe a property manager, while khawl are followers.
TABRISI:6:94#2/r5.anchor: وخوله الله أعطاه مالا وفلان خولي مال وخال مال وخائل مال إذا كان يصلح المال

TABRISI:6:94#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:94#2/r6.claim: Zaʿm may report something true or false; a poet’s example illustrates a claim presented as true.
TABRISI:6:94#2/r6.anchor: والزعم قد يكون حقا وقد يكون باطلا

TABRISI:6:94#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:94#2/r7.claim: Al-bayn is the verbal noun of bāna, to part; Abu Zayd says bāna al-ḥayy baynūna or baynan when people depart and separate.
TABRISI:6:94#2/r7.anchor: والبين مصدر بأن يبين إذا فارق

TABRISI:6:94#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:94#2/r8.claim: Furādā is accusative as a circumstantial phrase, and mā khawwalnākum is a relative construction functioning as the object of taraktum.
TABRISI:6:94#2/r8.anchor: فرادى نصب على الحال وما خولناكم موصول وصلة في موضع نصب بأنه مفعول تركتم

TABRISI:6:94#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94#2/r9.speaker: عكرمة
TABRISI:6:94#2/r9.claim: Ikrima says the verse was revealed about al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Kalada, who had claimed al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā would intercede for him.
TABRISI:6:94#2/r9.anchor: نزلت في النضر بن الحرث بن كلدة حين قال سوف يشفع لي اللات والعزى عن عكرمة

TABRISI:6:94#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94#2/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:94#2/r10.claim: One view takes this as God addressing His servants either at death or at resurrection.
TABRISI:6:94#2/r10.anchor: قيل هذا من كلام الله تعالى يخاطب به عباده إما عند الموت أو عند البعث

TABRISI:6:94#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94#2/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:94#2/r11.claim: Another view says angels convey these words from God to those whose souls they take.
TABRISI:6:94#2/r11.anchor: وقيل: هو من كلام الملائكة يؤدونه عن الله إلى الذين يقبضون أرواحهم

TABRISI:6:94#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94#2/r12.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:6:94#2/r12.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī glosses furādā as arriving alone, without wealth, dependents, children, or household.
TABRISI:6:94#2/r12.anchor: وحدانا لا مال لكم ولا خول ولا ولد ولا حشم عن الجبائي

TABRISI:6:94#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94#2/r13.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:6:94#2/r13.claim: Al-Hasan glosses furādā as coming one by one, separately.
TABRISI:6:94#2/r13.anchor: واحدا واحدا على حدة عن الحسن

TABRISI:6:94#2/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94#2/r14.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:6:94#2/r14.claim: Al-Zajjāj says each person comes separated from a partner in wrongdoing and a brother or companion.
TABRISI:6:94#2/r14.anchor: كل واحد منهم منفردا من شريكة في الغي وشقيقه عن الزجاج

TABRISI:6:94#2/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94#2/r15.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:6:94#2/r15.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī explains the comparison as creation in the mothers’ wombs, without a defender or helper.
TABRISI:6:94#2/r15.anchor: كما خلقناكم في بطون أمهاتكم فلا ناصر لكم ولا معين عن الجبائي

TABRISI:6:94#2/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94#2/r16.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:6:94#2/r16.claim: The Prophet says people will be gathered barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised; Aisha worries that men and women will see one another, and he replies that each person will be occupied with his own affair.
TABRISI:6:94#2/r16.anchor: ما روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

TABRISI:6:94#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:94#3/r1.claim: The gifts are worldly possessions people prized; they leave them behind, bear their sins, and others enjoy what they left while they are held to account.
TABRISI:6:94#3/r1.anchor: معناه ملكناكم في الدنيا مما كنتم تتباهون به من الأموال { وراء ظهوركم } أي خلف ظهوركم في الدنيا

TABRISI:6:94#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94#3/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:94#3/r2.claim: The supposed intercessors are idols people expected to intercede for them before God on the Day of Resurrection.
TABRISI:6:94#3/r2.anchor: ليس معكم من كنتم تزعمون أنهم يشفعون لكم عند الله يوم القيامة وهي الأصنام

TABRISI:6:94#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94#3/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:94#3/r3.claim: They claimed the idols were God’s partners concerning them and their intercessors; worshipping them brings no benefit.
TABRISI:6:94#3/r3.anchor: زعمتم أنهم شركاؤنا فيكم وشفعاؤكم يريد وما نفعكم عبادة الأوثان التي كنتم تقولون

TABRISI:6:94#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94#3/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:94#3/r4.claim: The warning generalizes to everyone who worships or relies on anything besides God, hoping for benefit or fearing harm while disobeying God.
TABRISI:6:94#3/r4.anchor: وهذا عام في كل من عبد غير الله واعتمد غيره يرجو خيره ويخاف ضيره في مخالفة الله

TABRISI:6:94#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94#3/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:94#3/r5.claim: With bayn in the nominative, the severed thing is the bond that united them; with the accusative, their affair or bond was severed between them.
TABRISI:6:94#3/r5.anchor: أي وصلكم وجمعكم ومن قرأ بالنصب فمعناه لقد تقطع الأمر بينكم أو تقطع وصلكم بينكم

TABRISI:6:94#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94#3/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:94#3/r6.claim: Their supposed gods have vanished; they do not know where their intercessors went, and worshipping them has not helped.
TABRISI:6:94#3/r6.anchor: ضاع وتلاشى ولا تدرون أين ذهب من جعلتم شفعاءكم من آلهتكم ولم تنفعكم عبادتها

TABRISI:6:94#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94#3/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:94#3/r7.claim: Another interpretation takes the lost claim to be their denial of resurrection and recompense.
TABRISI:6:94#3/r7.anchor: وقيل: معناه ما تزعمون من عدم البعث والجزاء

TABRISI:6:94#3/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:94#3/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:94#3/r8.claim: The verse urges people to acquire obedience that brings salvation rather than wealth that must be left behind and cannot benefit them after death.
TABRISI:6:94#3/r8.anchor: قد حث الله سبحانه في هذه الآية على اقتناء الطاعات التي بها ينال الفوز وتدرك النجاة دون اقتناء المال

THALABI:v4p170/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p170/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p170/r9.claim: On Judgment Day people come singly and without their wealth, spouse, children, servants, or retinue.
THALABI:v4p170/r9.anchor: ولقد جئتمونا فرادى هذا خبر من الله تعالى أنه يقول للكفار يوم القيامة: ولقد جئتمونا فرادى وحدانا

THALABI:v4p170/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p170/r10.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v4p170/r10.claim: Al-Hasan explains فرادى as each person arriving alone, one by one.
THALABI:v4p170/r10.anchor: قال الحسن: ولقد جئتمونا فرادى كل واحدة على حدة

THALABI:v4p170/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p170/r11.speaker: ابن كيسان
THALABI:v4p170/r11.claim: Ibn Kaysan interprets فرادى as separated from the beings they worshipped.
THALABI:v4p170/r11.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان: مفردين من المعبودين، وفرادى جمع فردان مثل سكران وسكارى

THALABI:v4p170/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p170/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p170/r12.claim: فرادى is a plural of فردان, like سكران/سكارى and كسلان/كسالى; the singular may be pronounced with rāʾ sukūn, kasra, or fatḥa, and also as أفرد.
THALABI:v4p170/r12.anchor: وفرد بكسرها وفرد بالفتح وأفرد وجمعها أفراد مثل أحاد وفريد وفردان

THALABI:v4p170/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p170/r13.speaker: الأعرج
THALABI:v4p170/r13.claim: Al-Aʿraj reads فردي without the alif, like كسرى and كسلى.
THALABI:v4p170/r13.anchor: وقرأ الأعرج: فردي بغير ألف مثل كسرى [وكسلى]

THALABI:v4p170/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p170/r14.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p170/r14.claim: People return as they were first created: barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised.
THALABI:v4p170/r14.anchor: كما خلقناكم أول مرة عراة حفاة غرلا بهم

THALABI:v4p170/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p170/r15.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p170/r15.claim: خولناكم means We gave you and empowered you with wealth, children, and servants, which you leave behind in the world.
THALABI:v4p170/r15.anchor: وتركتم وخلفتم ما خولناكم أعطيناكم ومكناكم من الأموال والأولاد والخدم وراء ظهوركم

THALABI:v4p171/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p171/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v4p171/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that after the resurrection blast souls fill the space between heaven and earth like bees, return to their bodies through the nostrils, and people emerge barefoot, naked, uncircumcised, and wait for judgment; the Prophet is first to emerge.
THALABI:v4p171/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «ينفخ نفخة البعث فتخرج الأرواح كأنها النحل قد ملئت ما بين السماء والأرض

THALABI:v4p171/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p171/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v4p171/r2.claim: A report from Aisha says that on that day each person is occupied by his or her own affair; men do not look at women, nor women at men.
THALABI:v4p171/r2.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لكل امرئ منهم يومئذ شأن يغنيه لا ينظر الرجال إلى النساء

THALABI:v4p171/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p171/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p171/r3.claim: The alleged intercessors are the idols that polytheists claimed were partners of God and would intercede for them.
THALABI:v4p171/r3.anchor: وما نرى معكم شفعاءكم الذين زعمتم أنهم فيكم شركاء وذلك إن المشركين زعموا أنهم يعبدون الأصنام

THALABI:v4p171/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p171/r4.speaker: أهل المدينة، والحسن، ومجاهد، وأبو رجاء، والكسائي
THALABI:v4p171/r4.claim: The Medinese, Hasan, Mujahid, Abu Rajaʾ, and al-Kisaʾi read بينكم in the accusative.
THALABI:v4p171/r4.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة، والحسن، ومجاهد، وأبو رجاء، والكسائي: بينكم نصبا

THALABI:v4p171/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p171/r5.speaker: أهل المدينة، والحسن، ومجاهد
THALABI:v4p171/r5.claim: The Medinese, Hasan, and Mujahid also read the phrase as ما بينكم, a reading attributed as well to Ubayy and Abd Allah.
THALABI:v4p171/r5.anchor: وقرأ أهل المدينة، والحسن، ومجاهد: وهي قراءة أبي موسى الأشعري على معنى لقد تقطع ما بينكم وكذلك هو في قراءة عبد الله

THALABI:v4p171/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p171/r6.speaker: الباقون
THALABI:v4p171/r6.claim: The remaining readers use the nominative, understood as your bond being severed.
THALABI:v4p171/r6.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: بالرفع على معنى لقد تقطع وصلكم

THALABI:v4p171/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p171/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p171/r7.claim: بين is an opposite meaning word that can signify either connection or separation; the author cites a poetic line about separation and love.
THALABI:v4p171/r7.anchor: فالبين من الأضداد يكفي وصلا وهجرا وأنشد: لعمرك لولا البين لا يقطع الهوى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r1.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r1.claim: Semanticists offer two readings of the past tense: it may quote what people are told in the Hereafter, as the preceding verse does, or express the future in past form to affirm its certainty.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r1.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: (هذا يكون على وجهين أحدهما: أنه على الحكاية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r2.claim: Al-Farra calls furada a plural, notes that Arabs also say furadiya, and says it is indeclinable by analogy with thulatha and rubaʿ; its singular forms include fard, farid, fard, and fardan.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r3.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r3.claim: Al-Layth says fard is something alone; afrad means to make one, and people come furada or count nuts and coins one by one as afrād.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r3.anchor: وقال الليث: (الفرد: ما كان وحده، يقال: فرد يفرد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r4.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r4.claim: Ibn Qutayba parses furada as the plural of fardan, like sukkaran becoming sukara and kaslan becoming kusala.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r5.speaker: غيره
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r5.claim: Another grammarian derives furada as the plural of farid, on the pattern of radif and ridafa.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r5.anchor: وقال غيره: (فرادى جمع فريد مثل رديف وردافى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says they come with no family, property, children, or anything they had sent ahead.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r6.anchor: بلا أهل ولا مال ولا ولد ولا شيء قدمتموه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r7.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r7.claim: Al-Hasan glosses furada as each person coming alone, separately.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r7.anchor: وقال الحسن: (فرادى كل واحد على حدة)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r8.speaker: ابن كيسان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r8.claim: Ibn Kaysan says they come isolated from what they worshipped and from those who used to support them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r8.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان (¬8): (ولقد جئتمونا مفردين مما كنتم تعبدون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r9.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r9.claim: Abu Ishaq likewise says each person is separated from his partner in misguidance and accomplice.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p293/r9.anchor: ونحو ذلك قال أبو إسحاق قال: (كل واحد منفرد عن شريكه في الغي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p295/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p295/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p295/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says they come barefoot and naked, as they emerged from their mothers' wombs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p295/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد: حفاة عراة كما خرجتم من بطون أمهاتكم)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p295/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p295/r2.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p295/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj offers another possible sense: just as God began you the first time, so your resurrection is like your creation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p295/r2.anchor: وذكر الزجاج وجها آخر تحتمله اللغة: (كما بدأناكم أول مرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p295/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p295/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p295/r3.claim: Khawwalnakum means gave you ownership; khawl denotes the servants and blessings God grants a person.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p295/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p295/r4.speaker: أبو النجم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p295/r4.claim: Abu al-Najm's phrase kom al-dhura min khawl al-mukhawwil supplies poetic evidence for khawl as a grant or possession.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p295/r4.anchor: قال أبو النجم (¬6): كوم الذرى من خول المخول

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p295/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p295/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p295/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas specifies the abandoned gifts as comforts, wealth, servants, estates, and livestock.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p295/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: {وتركتم ما خولناكم}: (يريد: من النعيم والمال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p295/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p295/r6.speaker: ابن عباس والمفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p295/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says the idols were alleged partners of God; exegetes explain that polytheists worshipped them as God's partners and intercessors with Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p295/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد: شركاء لي) (¬3) و {شفعاءكم}، قال المفسرون (¬4):

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p296/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p296/r1.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p296/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj prefers the nominative baynu-kum, meaning the bond between you broke; the accusative is also allowed and means your association was severed.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p296/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p296/r2.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p296/r2.claim: Abu Ali says bayn can be a declinable noun or an adverb; the nominative reading treats the adverb as a noun, supported by its use in 41:5 and 18:78 and in Muhalhil's line. It cannot be a verbal noun meaning separation, since that would yield the wrong sense of 'your separation has separated.'
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p296/r2.anchor: قال أبو علي: (هذا الاسم يستعمل على ضربين: أحدهما: أن يكون اسما متصرفا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p296/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p296/r3.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p296/r3.claim: Abu Ali explains the shift: between people who share kinship, friendship, or partnership can function like a bond, so its severance means their bond has broken; Sibawayh's example also supports nominal use.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p296/r3.anchor: لما استعمل مع الشيئين المتلابسين في نحو: بيني وبينه شركة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p296/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p296/r4.speaker: مهلهل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p296/r4.claim: Muhalhil's poem uses bayn as a noun for the distance between the two sides of a well, supporting Abu Ali's grammatical analysis.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p296/r4.anchor: وقال (¬2) مهلهل (¬3): كأن رماحهم أشطان بئر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p296/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p296/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p296/r5.claim: One analysis of the accusative reading supplies an omitted subject from the preceding mention of alleged partners: their bond among you has been severed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p296/r5.anchor: فأما من قرأ: {لقد تقطع بينكم} بالنصب ففيه مذهبان أحدهما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p300/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p300/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p300/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses what has broken between them as their bond and affection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p300/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: {لقد تقطع بينكم} (يريد: وصلكم ومودتكم)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p300/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p300/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p300/r2.claim: Muqatil says the relations they maintained with one another have ended.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p300/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: {لقد تقطع بينكم} (يعني: ما تواصلتم بينكم)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p300/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p300/r3.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p300/r3.claim: Al-Hasan glosses the phrase as the matter between them having been broken off.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p300/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p300/r4.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p300/r4.claim: Qatada says it means whatever bond existed between them.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p300/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p300/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p300/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says their claims have vanished: what they used to lie about in worldly life is gone.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p300/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (ذهب عنكم ما كنتم تكذبون في الدنيا)

QASHANI:6:93-94#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:93-94#2/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:93-94#2/r1.claim: People arrive alone, stripped of traits, attachments, family, and individual existence through absorption in the unity of the essence.
QASHANI:6:93-94#2/r1.anchor: مجردين عن الصفات والعلائق والأهل والأقارب والوجود بالاستغراق في عين جمع الذات

QASHANI:6:93-94#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:93-94#2/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:93-94#2/r2.claim: The first creation is the origination of individual identities in eternity when the primordial covenant was taken.
QASHANI:6:93-94#2/r2.anchor: بإنشاء ذرات هوياتكم في الأزل عند أخذ الميثاق

QASHANI:6:93-94#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:93-94#2/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:93-94#2/r3.claim: What God granted and they leave behind includes worldly means, knowledge, and virtues.

QASHANI:6:93-94#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:93-94#2/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:93-94#2/r4.claim: Their supposed intercessors are the means, causes, beloved objects, and idols to which they attached themselves and attributed influence.
QASHANI:6:93-94#2/r4.anchor: وسائلكم وأسبابكم وما آثرتموه بهواكم وتعلقتم بها من محبوباتكم ومعبوداتكم

QASHANI:6:93-94#2/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:93-94#2/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:93-94#2/r5.claim: The supposed independent entities vanish when all things are witnessed in God.
QASHANI:6:93-94#2/r5.anchor: شيئا موجودا بشهودكم ثناء الكل في الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r1.claim: On Resurrection, unbelievers come alone, without family, property, or anything they sent ahead.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r1.anchor: { ولقد جئتمونا فرادى } يقال للكفار في الآخرة: جئتمونا فرادى بلا أهل، ولا مال، ولا شيء قدمتموه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r2.claim: They return as they were first created, like emerging from their mothers' wombs; they have left behind the wealth and livestock God gave them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r2.anchor: { كما خلقناكم أول مرة } كما خرجتم من بطون أمهاتكم { وتركتم ما خولناكم } ملكناكم وأعطيناكم من المال والعبيد والمواشي

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r3.claim: The alleged intercessors and partners were idols that polytheists worshipped as God's partners and their intercessors.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r3.anchor: كانوا يعبدون الأصنام على أنهم شركاء الله وشفعاؤهم عنده

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r4.claim: Their bonds and affection have been severed, and their false worldly claims have vanished.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:94-95/r4.anchor: { لقد تقطع بينكم } وصلكم ومودتكم { وضل عنكم } ذهب عنكم { ما كنتم تزعمون } تكذبون في الدنيا.

ELMALILI:6:93-94/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:93-94/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:93-94/r7.claim: At resurrection each person comes alone, just as created the first time, having left behind all the possessions God had granted.
ELMALILI:6:93-94/r7.anchor: bugün bize ilk defa sizi halk ettiğimiz gibi teker teker, yalnız başınıza geldiniz

ELMALILI:6:93-94/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:93-94/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:93-94/r8.claim: The supposed intercessors are absent; people had imagined them partners in their existence, holding a share in lordship and interceding for them with God.
ELMALILI:6:93-94/r8.anchor: Mevcûdiyetiniz üzerinde bunların rubûbiyet hissesine mâlik birtakım şürekâ olduklarını ve Allah’a karşı size şefaat edeceklerini zannediyordunuz

ELMALILI:6:93-94/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:93-94/r9.speaker: نافع، حفص، كسائي، أبو جعفر
ELMALILI:6:93-94/r9.claim: Readers other than Nafi, Hafs, Kisai, and Abu Ja‘far read baynakum with the nūn raised; the author renders this as the permanent severing of all ties between them.
ELMALILI:6:93-94/r9.anchor: Nâfi‘, Hafs, Kisâî, Ebû Cafer’den mâ‘adâsında nûn’un ref‘iyle بَيْنَكُمْ okunduğuna göre

ELMALILI:6:93-94/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:93-94/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:93-94/r10.claim: The address declares that the bonds between them have been severed forever and their former imagined supports have vanished.
ELMALILI:6:93-94/r10.anchor: artık aranız ebediyyen açıldı, bütün râbıtalar kesildi, târumâr oldu

ELMALILI:6:93-94/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:93-94/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:93-94/r11.claim: The imagined partners and intercessors prove to be delusions that have disappeared from them.
ELMALILI:6:93-94/r11.anchor: zu‘m etmiş olduğunuz o hayaller, o kuruntular sizden gayb oldu gitti

ELMALILI:6:93-94/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:93-94/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:93-94/r12.claim: People should picture this reckoning and avoid injustice and failure to recognize God’s due.
ELMALILI:6:93-94/r12.anchor: Bunları göz önüne getirmeli de Allah’a karşı haksızlıkta, takdirsizlikte bulunmamalıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:94/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:94/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:94/r1.claim: At the Resurrection, unbelievers stand alone and helpless before God; relatives, friends, wealth, status, and the beings they worshiped will not help, and the things they hoped would aid them disappear.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:94/r1.anchor: İnkârcıların âhirette, mutlak güç ve hâkimiyet sahibi olan Allah karşısındaki yalnızlık ve çaresizliklerinin anlatıldığı âyete göre onların dünyadaki akraba ve dostları

BURHAN:v4p257/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p257/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p257/r9.claim: The author rejects al-Basīṭ's and Ibn Mālik's claim that Qur'anic bal only marks transition, since the Qur'an also uses it to retract and correct.
BURHAN:v4p257/r9.anchor: وزعم صاحب البسيط وابن مالك أنها لا تقع في القرآن إلا بهذا المعنى وليست كذلك

BURHAN:v4p403/r13.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p403/r13.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p403/r13.claim: Mā can be elided in expressions such as 'when you see there', 'this is a separation between me and you', and 'what was between you was severed'.
BURHAN:v4p403/r13.anchor: فائدة قال بعضهم وقد تجىء ما مضمرة

SULAMI:v1p209#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p209#4/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p209#4/r1.claim: Some say the servant's highest station is to acknowledge complete insolvency and return to God empty of all acts of obedience.
SULAMI:v1p209#4/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : أجل مقامات العبد إظهار إفلاسه والرجوع إليه خاليا من جميع طاعاته

SULAMI:v1p209#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p209#4/r2.speaker: أبو حفص
SULAMI:v1p209#4/r2.claim: Asked what he could bring before God, Abu Hafs answered that a poor person can offer only poverty to the Rich; he reads arriving alone as being empty of works, states, and devotions.
SULAMI:v1p209#4/r2.anchor: قيل لأبي حفص : بماذا تقدم على الله

ITQAN:v2p466#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p466#2/r1.speaker: الراغب
ITQAN:v2p466#2/r1.claim: Al-Raghib defines بين as the gap or middle between two things; it can function as an adverb or a noun and normally requires multiple referents or repeated singulars.
ITQAN:v2p466#2/r1.anchor: قال الراغب هي موضوعة للخلل بين الشيئين ووسطهما

ITQAN:v2p466#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p466#2/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p466#2/r2.claim: The phrase لقد تقطع بينكم is read accusatively as an adverb or nominatively as a verbal noun meaning connection.
ITQAN:v2p466#2/r2.anchor: بالنصب على أنه ظرف وبالرفع على أنه اسم مصدر بمعنى الوصل

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p103/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p103/r1.speaker: عكرمة
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p103/r1.claim: Ikrima reports that al-Nadr ibn al-Harith claimed al-Lat and al-Uzza would intercede for him, and the verse was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p103/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة قال قال النضر بن الحرث سوف تشفع إلى اللات والعزي فنزلت هذه الآية

FARRA:v1p345/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p345/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p345/r3.claim: فرادى is plural; its singular forms include فرد، فرد، and فريد, while فراد is also a plural and فرد is not used with this plural sense.
FARRA:v1p345/r3.anchor: وهو جمع. والعرب تقول: [قوم ] فرادى وفراد يا هذا

FARRA:v1p345/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p345/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p345/r4.claim: Arabs leave فرادى and فراد indeclinable, by analogy with ثلاث and رباع.

FARRA:v1p345/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p345/r5.speaker: بعضهم
FARRA:v1p345/r5.claim: An anonymous poet uses فراد and مثنى as contrasting groupings, witnessing the usage of فراد.
FARRA:v1p345/r5.anchor:
وأنشدني بعضهم:
ترى النعرات الزرق تحت لبانه ... فراد ومثنى

FARRA:v1p345/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p345/r6.speaker: حمزة ومجاهد
FARRA:v1p345/r6.claim: Ḥamza and Mujāhid read بينكم, which Farrāʾ explains as your bond or connection.
FARRA:v1p345/r6.anchor: قرأ حمزة ومجاهد بينكم يريد وصلكم

FARRA:v1p345/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p345/r7.speaker: عبد الله
FARRA:v1p345/r7.claim: ʿAbd Allāh's reading ما بينكم is, in Farrāʾ's view, the more idiomatic construction.
FARRA:v1p345/r7.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله لقد تقطع ما بينكم وهو وجه الكلام

FARRA:v1p345/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p345/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p345/r8.claim: When the verb governs بين by itself, بين is accusative even where it has a syntactic role otherwise associated with nominative; when isolated, it declines normally.
FARRA:v1p345/r8.anchor: إذا جعل الفعل لبين ترك نصبا كما قالوا: أتاني دونك من الرجال

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p157/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p157/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p157/r1.claim: Furādā is a plural of fard, apparently formed like kaslā from kaslān and sukarā from sakrān.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p157/r1.anchor: {فرادى} جمع فرد. وكأنه جمع فردان. كما قيل: كسلان وكسالى وسكران وسكارى.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p157/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p157/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p157/r2.claim: Khawwalnākum means that God made the possessions theirs or granted them ownership.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p157/r2.anchor: {وتركتم ما خولناكم وراء ظهوركم} أي: ملكناكم.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p157/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p157/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p157/r3.claim: The alleged partners were claimed to share with God in creating the people.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p157/r3.anchor: {الذين زعمتم أنهم فيكم شركاء} أي زعمتم أنهم لي في خلقكم شركاء.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p157/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p157/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p157/r4.claim: The ties severed are the kinship, alliance, and affection that bound them in worldly life.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p157/r4.anchor: {لقد تقطع بينكم} أي تقطعت الوصل التي كانت بينكم في الدنيا من القرابة والحلف والمودة.

NAHHAS:v2p82/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p82/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p82/r5.claim: Furādā is a circumstantial accusative and is indeclinable because it ends in the feminine alif.
NAHHAS:v2p82/r5.anchor: في موضع نصب على الحال ولم ينصرف لأن فيه ألف تأنيث

NAHHAS:v2p82/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p82/r6.speaker: أبو حيوة
NAHHAS:v2p82/r6.claim: Abu Haywa reads furādan with tanwīn; Harun identifies it as Tamimi, while other dialect reports include furād with or without tanwīn.
NAHHAS:v2p82/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة ( فرادا ) بالتنوين قال هارون لغة تميم

NAHHAS:v2p82/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p82/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p82/r7.claim: People come to God alone, without the allies who shared their error to help them.
NAHHAS:v2p82/r7.anchor: قال أبو جعفر المعنى ولقد جئتمونا منفردين ليس معكم ناصر

NAHHAS:v2p82/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p82/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p82/r8.claim: Three explanations are offered: people are alone as at first creation, naked, or restored as they were first created.
NAHHAS:v2p82/r8.anchor: فيه ثلاثة أقوال يكون منفردين كما خلقوا ويكون عراة

NAHHAS:v2p82/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p82/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p82/r9.claim: The alleged intercessors are those worshipped as partners and assigned a share of people’s wealth.
NAHHAS:v2p82/r9.anchor: أي الذين عبدتموهم وجعلتموهم شركاء في أموالكم

NAHHAS:v2p82/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p82/r10.speaker: أبو عمرو
NAHHAS:v2p82/r10.claim: Abu Amr takes the phrase to mean that the bond between them has been severed; baynakum is adverbial.
NAHHAS:v2p82/r10.anchor: قال أبو عمرو أي وصلكم و ( بينكم ) على الظرف

SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r1.claim: Furādā is accusative as a circumstantial phrase describing the subject of “you came to Us.”
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r1.anchor: منصوب على الحال من فاعل " جئتمونا "

SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r2.claim: The past verb may express a future event assured to happen, as with “God’s command has come” and “the people of Paradise called.”
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r2.anchor: أنه بمعنى المستقبل أي: تجيئوننا، وإنما أبرزه في صورة الماضي لتحققه كقوله تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r3.claim: Alternatively, the verb is past and depicts the scene from the perspective of the day they are told this, when their coming is already past.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r3.anchor: أنه ماض والمراد به حكاية الحال بين يدي الله تعالى يوم يقال لهم ذلك

SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r4.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ allows furādā to be a plural of several forms: fard, farīd, fard, and fardān.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r4.anchor: فقال الفراء: " فرادى جمع فرد وفريد وفرد وفردان "

SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r5.speaker: ابن قتيبة
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r5.claim: Ibn Qutayba derives it as the plural of fardān, on the pattern of sukkārā from sukkārān and ʿujālā from ʿajlān.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r5.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة: " هو جمع فردان ك سكران وسكارى، وعجلان وعجالى "

SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r6.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r6.claim: Al-Rāghib reports the derivation as plural of farīd, like radīf/radāfā and asīr/asārā.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r6.anchor: هو جمع فريد كرديف وردافى، وأسير وأسارى، قاله الراغب

SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r7.claim: Others derive it from fard with either a fatḥa or sukūn on the rāʾ; on this account its alif is feminine like those in sukkārā and asārā, so it is diptote.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r7.anchor: وقيل: هو جمع فرد بفتح الراء، وقيل بسكونها، وعلى هذا فألفه للتأنيث

SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r8.claim: Some classify it as a collective noun because fard does not regularly form this plural; those calling it a plural mean that semantically, “one by one.”
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r8.anchor: لأن فردا لا يجمع على فرادى

SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r9.claim: The expression means “one by one”; an anonymous poetic line uses furādā alongside “in pairs” as evidence for this sense.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r9.anchor: ومعنى فرادى: فردا فردا، فإذا قلت: جاء القوم فرادى

SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r10.claim: Related usage includes farada yaf rudu furūdan, fārid, afrad, and feminine fardāʾ; its plural is fard, like ḥumr from aḥmar/aḥmarāʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r10.anchor: ويقال: فرد يفرد فرودا فهو فارد وأفردته أنا، ورجل أفرد

SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r11.speaker: عيسى بن عمر وأبو حيوة
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r11.claim: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and Abū Ḥaywa read furādan, the declinable form used in Tamīm.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r11.anchor: وهي لغة تميم، وبها قرأ عيسى بن عمر وأبو حيوة

SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r12.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r12.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ records a rare anomalous reading with tanwīn, treating فراد as a sound noun, a rare plural like nuwwām and rijāl.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r12.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء " وقرئ في الشاذ بالتنوين على أنه اسم صحيح

SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r13.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r13.claim: Another anomalous reading is فراد without tanwīn, indeclinable like aḥād and rubāʿ as a shifted adjective.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r13.anchor: ويقال أيضا: " جاء القوم فراد " غير منصرف فهو كأحاد

SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r14.speaker: خارجة عن نافع وأبي عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r14.claim: Khārija reports that Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr read fardā, analogizing the group to a feminine collective as in “you see people drunk.”
SAMIN-DURR:6:94/r14.anchor: وروى خارجة عن نافع وأبي عمرو كليهما أنهما قرآ " فردى " مثل سكرى

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#2/r1.claim: The kāf may be circumstantial to the subject of “you came to Us”; grammarians who reject multiple circumstances instead treat it as a substitute for furādā.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#2/r1.anchor: أنها منصوبة المحل على الحال من فاعل " جئتمونا "

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#2/r2.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#2/r2.claim: A second analysis makes the kāf an adjective of an omitted verbal noun; Makkī estimates “coming singly, a singleness like your state when first created.”
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#2/r2.anchor: وقدره مكي: " منفردين انفرادا/ مثل حالكم أول مرة "

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#2/r3.claim: Al-Samīn prefers the direct circumstantial analysis because the verb indicates its verbal noun more strongly than a descriptive word does.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#2/r3.anchor: والأول أحسن لأن دلالة الفعل على المصدر أقوى

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#2/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#2/r4.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ makes the kāf circumstantial to the implicit subject of furādā, estimating “resembling your initial creation.”
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#2/r4.anchor: كذا قدره أبو البقاء، وفيه نظر

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#2/r5.claim: Al-Samīn objects that they do not resemble their initial creation; the estimate should supply “your state” as the comparison.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#2/r5.anchor: وصوابه أن تقدر مضافا أي: مشبهة حالكم حال ابتداء خلقكم

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#2/r6.claim: Awwala marratin is a time adverb governed by khalaqnākum; marra was originally the verbal noun of marra yamurru, then broadened to mean a time.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#2/r6.anchor: منصوب على ظرف الزمان والعامل فيه

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#2/r7.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#2/r7.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ says the usage shows how closely a time expression resembles a verb.

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#2/r8.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#2/r8.claim: The Shaykh rejects treating marra as “the first creation,” since that implies a second creation; the event is a return or recreation.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#2/r8.anchor: وقال الشيخ: " وانتصب " أول مرة " على الظرف أي: أول زمان

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#3/r1.claim: Wa-taraktum may be an accusative circumstantial clause with an implicit qad, or an independent clause with no syntactic position.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#3/r1.anchor: أحدهما: أنها في محل نصب على الحال من فاعل " جئتمونا "

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#3/r2.claim: Mā is the object of taraka; min is a relative pronoun, while treating it as an indefinite noun with an omitted resumptive is weaker.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#3/r2.anchor: ويضعف جعلها نكرة موصوفة والعائد محذوف

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#3/r3.claim: Taraka takes one object here because it means “leave”; if given the sense “make,” it would take two objects.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#3/r3.anchor: ولو ضمنت معنى صير تعدت لاثنين

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#3/r4.claim: Khawwala takes two objects because it means to give and grant possession.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#3/r4.anchor: يتعدى لاثنين لأنه بمعنى أعطى وملك

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#3/r5.claim: Al-khawl means the blessings God granted; khawwalkahu means “I gave him ownership of the khawl,” like mawaltuhu al-māl.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#3/r5.anchor: والخول: ما أعطاه الله من النعم

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#3/r6.speaker: أبو النجم
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#3/r6.claim: Abū al-Najm’s verse uses khawl in the phrase khawli al-mukhawwal as lexical evidence.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#3/r6.anchor: قال أبو النجم: 1988 كوم الذرى من خول

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#3/r7.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#3/r7.claim: Al-Rāghib says takhwīl originally means giving khawl; alternatively it is giving what becomes one’s responsibility or what needs caretaking.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#3/r7.anchor: وقال الراغب: " والتخويل في الأصل: إعطاء الخول

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r1.claim: Warāʾa ẓuhūrikum attaches to taraktum; alternatively, taraka means “made,” taking the relative object and this locative as its two objects.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r1.anchor: ويجوز أن يضمن " ترك " هنا معنى صير

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r2.claim: On the second parsing, the meaning is that they made what God granted them into something left behind their backs.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r2.anchor: أي: وصيرتم الترك الذي خولناكموه كائنا وراء ظهوركم

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r3.claim: The apparent reading of narā is visual perception taking one object, with maʿakum attached to it.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r3.anchor: الظاهر أنها المتعدية لواحد فهي بصرية

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r4.claim: Narā could instead mean “know,” taking two objects; the second would be a locative meaning “present with you.”
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون بمعنى علم، فيتعدى لاثنين

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r5.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ considers the “know” analysis weak because “we do not know your intercessors with you” is not intended.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r5.anchor: إلا أن أبا البقاء استضعف هذا الوجه وهو كما قال

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r6.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r6.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ rejects taking maʿakum as circumstantial to the intercessors, which he thinks would mean they are present but unseen.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r6.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " ولا يجوز أن يكون أي معكم حالا من الشفعاء

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r7.claim: Al-Samīn replies that negating a qualified entity can deny either the entity itself or only its qualification; the wording need not mean the intercessors are present but unseen.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r7.anchor: وذلك أن النفي إذا دخل على ذات بقيد ففيه وجهان

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r8.claim: Al-Samīn points to his earlier treatment of this construction in the opening of al-Baqara and at “they do not ask people persistently.”
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r8.anchor: وقد تقدم تحقيق هذه القاعدة في أوائل البقرة وفي قوله

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r9.claim: The clause anna-hum fills both object slots of zaʿamtum, and fīkum attaches to shurakāʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r9.anchor: و " أنهم " ساد مسد المفعولين ل " زعم "

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r10.claim: The alleged intercessors are said to be partners with God concerning the people’s worship or creation, since the people associated them with God in both.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r10.anchor: والمعنى: الذين زعمتم أنهم شركاء لله فيكم أي: في عبادتكم

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r11.claim: One proposed reading takes fī as “with” or “in the presence of,” but al-Samīn says it is unnecessary.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r11.anchor: وقيل " في " بمعنى " عند " ولا حاجة إليه

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r12.claim: Another explanation makes them partners in the people’s punishment, sharing it if the people believed they would share their calamities.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r12.anchor: وقيل: المعنى أنهم يتحملون عنكم نصيبا من العذاب

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r13.speaker: نافع والكسائي وعاصم في رواية حفص
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r13.claim: Nāfiʿ, al-Kisāʾī, and ʿĀṣim in Ḥafṣ’s transmission read baynakum in the accusative; the rest read it in the nominative.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r13.anchor: قرأ نافع والكسائي وعاصم في رواية حفص عنه: " بينكم " نصبا

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r14.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r14.claim: For the accusative reading, the strongest analysis supplies an implicit subject meaning “connection,” inferred from the mention of partners; baynakum is adverbial.

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r15.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r15.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r15.claim: Al-Akhfash makes baynakum the subject while retaining its usual accusative form as an adverb; similar examples include 60:3 and 72:11.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#4/r15.anchor: على أغلب أحواله وهو مذهب الأخفش

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#5/r1.speaker: الواحدي
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#5/r1.claim: Al-Wāḥidī explains that an adverb frequently used in the accusative may retain that form when syntactically nominative.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#5/r1.anchor: قال الواحدي: " كما جرى في كلامهم منصوبا ظرفا، تركوه

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#5/r2.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#5/r2.claim: The Shaykh describes the word as built on its common adverbial form, but al-Samīn objects that frequency is not a recognized cause of indeclinability; the Shaykh also suggests annexation to an indeclinable word.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#5/r2.anchor: وفي كلام الشيخ لما حكى مذهب الأخفش ما يصرح بأنه مبني فإنه قال: " وخرجه الأخفش على أنه فاعل ولكنه مبني

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#5/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#5/r3.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ supplies an omitted subject described by baynakum, estimating “a connection between you has been severed.”
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#5/r3.anchor: أن الفاعل محذوف، و " بينكم " صفة له قامت مقامه

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#5/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#5/r4.claim: The Shaykh objects that a subject cannot be omitted; al-Samīn replies that Abū al-Baqāʾ means it is unexpressed while its substitute stands in its place.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#5/r4.anchor: ورده الشيخ بأن الفاعل لا يحذف

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#5/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#5/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#5/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya likewise supplies an omitted subject such as “connection” or “bond”; al-Samīn calls the analysis clear.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#5/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: " ويكون الفعل مسندا إلى شيء محذوف

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#5/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#5/r6.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#5/r6.claim: The Shaykh rejects Ibn ʿAṭiyya’s omitted-subject account on the grounds stated above.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#5/r6.anchor: ورده الشيخ بما تقدم. ويجاب عنه

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#5/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#5/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#5/r7.claim: A fourth analysis makes baynakum the subject, indeclinable because it is annexed to a nondeclinable word.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#5/r7.anchor: الرابع: أن " بينكم " هو الفاعل، وإنما بني لإضافته إلى غير متمكن

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#5/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#5/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#5/r8.claim: A poetic example keeps mithla fatḥa although it is attached to the nominative damm, illustrating this analysis.

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r1.claim: A second anonymous line has ghayra in the accusative form even though it is the subject of yamnaʿ.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r1.anchor: حمامة في غصون ذات أوقال بفتح " غير " وهي فاعل

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r2.speaker: النابغة
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r2.claim: Al-Nābigha’s line has maqālata with fatḥa though it substitutes for a nominative clause, because it is annexed to indeclinable أن and its clause.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r2.anchor: قول النابغة: 1991 أتاني أبيت اللعن أنك لمتني

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r3.claim: Both taqaṭṭaʿa and ḍalla seek “what you used to claim” as subject. Basrans prefer applying the later verb; Kufans prefer the earlier one.

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r4.speaker: البصريون
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r4.claim: On the Basran preference to apply the later verb, ḍalla raises mā; taqaṭṭaʿa receives an implicit subject and governs baynakum as an adverb.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r4.anchor: فعلى اختيار البصريين يكون " ضل " هو الرفع ل " ما كنتم تزعمون "

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r5.speaker: الكوفيون
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r5.claim: On the Kufan preference to apply the earlier verb, taqaṭṭaʿa raises mā and ḍalla has an implicit subject; baynakum remains an adverb governed by taqaṭṭaʿa.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r5.anchor: وعلى اختيار الكوفيين يكون " تقطع " هو الرافع ل " ما كنتم تزعمون "

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r6.speaker: الكوفيون
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r6.claim: A further analysis supplies a deleted relative noun, “what is between you”; Kufan grammarians allow this omission and cite Arabic poetry.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r6.anchor: أن الظرف صلة لموصول محذوف تقديره: تقطع ما بينكم

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r7.speaker: عبد الله ومجاهد والأعمش
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r7.claim: The reading “لقد تقطع ما بينكم” reported from ʿAbd Allāh, Mujāhid, and al-Aʿmash supports supplying the deleted relative noun.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r7.anchor: قراءة عبد الله ومجاهد والأعمش: { لقد تقطع ما بينكم }

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī paraphrases the clause as “the severing occurred between you,” construing the verb as predicated of its verbal noun by interpretation.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r8.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " لقد تقطع بينكم: لقد وقع التقطع بينكم

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r9.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r9.claim: The Shaykh objects that this requires deleting the subject or using a verb and subject with the same sense, lacking distinct predicate and subject.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r9.anchor: إلا أن الشيخ اعترض فقال: " وظاهره أنه ليس بجيد

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r10.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r10.claim: The Shaykh adds that “the severing severed” would also imply the opposite of the intended meaning, as if connection had resulted.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r10.anchor: أنه يلزم عليه أيضا فساد المعنى

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r11.claim: Al-Samīn says the Shaykh’s objection does not refute al-Zamakhsharī because the latter explicitly bases the parse on the stated interpretive paraphrase.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#6/r11.anchor: وهذا الذي أورده الشيخ وقررته من كلامه حتى فهم لا يرد

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r1.claim: On the second reading, بين is broadened from an adverb into a declinable noun and assigned the verb's action.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r1.anchor: فصار اسما كسائر الأسماء المتصرف فيها

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r2.claim: Qur'anic usage, Sibawayh, and poetry show بين used as an inflected noun, including in genitive constructions.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r2.anchor: وحكى سيبويه: " هو أحمر بين العينين "

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r3.speaker: عنترة
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r3.claim: Antarah's line uses بين in بين المنسمين as an inflected noun between camel foot joints.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r3.anchor:
وقال عنترة:
1994 وكأنما أقص الإكام عشية

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r4.speaker: مهلهل
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r4.claim: Muhalhil's line offers another inflected use of بين in بعيدة بين جاليها.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r4.anchor:
وقال مهلهل:
1995 كأن رماحنا أشطان بئر

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r5.claim: Another poetic example parses بينها as the subject of مخالف; it is built because it is annexed to an indeclinable word.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r5.anchor: يروى برفع " بينها " وفتحه على أنه فاعل

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r6.claim: Poetic examples use بينها and raised أمام and دون, illustrating inflected adverbial nouns.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r6.anchor: ومثله في ذلك: أمام ودون كقوله:

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن جني والمهدوي والزهراوي
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r7.claim: They take بين as a noun meaning connection; on this account it can denote either connection or separation, like الجون.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r7.anchor: ويعزى هذا لأبي عمرو وابن جني والمهدوي والزهراوي

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r8.speaker: أبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r8.claim: Abu Amr explains تقطع بينكم as your bond being severed; Abu Ubayd transmits his explanation.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r8.anchor: وكان أبو عمرو يقول: معنى تقطع بينكم: تقطع وصلكم

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r9.speaker: الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r9.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the raised reading is better and explains the phrase as your bond having been cut.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r9.anchor: وقال الزجاج: " والرفع أجود، ومعناه: لقد تقطع وصلكم

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r10.claim: Ibn Atiyya objects that Arabs do not attest بين meaning connection; he suggests either inference from this verse or figurative distance and separation.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r10.anchor: إلا أن ابن عطية طعن فيه وزعم أنه لم يسمع من العرب " البين " بمعنى الوصل

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r11.claim: The author rejects Ibn Atiyya's objection: the named authorities are reliable, and Abu Amr's report alone would suffice to establish the usage.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r11.anchor: لأن أبا عمرو وأبا عبيد وابن جني والزهراوي والمهدوي والزجاج أئمة

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r12.speaker: الفارسي
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r12.claim: Al-Farisi explains the connection sense metaphorically: بين came to signify bonds such as partnership and kinship, making metaphor preferable to homonymy.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#7/r12.anchor: ووجه المجاز كما قاله الفارسي: أنه لما استعمل " بين " مع الشيئين المتلابسين

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#8/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#8/r1.speaker: أبو علي
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#8/r1.claim: Abu Ali argues that raised بين is the adverb broadened into a noun, not a verbal noun meaning separation, which would yield the unsuitable sense your separation was severed.
