SAMIN-DURR:6:94#8/r1.anchor: وقال أبو علي أيضا: " ويدل على أن هذا المرفوع هو الذي استعمل ظرفا

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#8/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#8/r2.speaker: أبو عبيد
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#8/r2.claim: Abu Ubayd reads بين in the nominative, citing Arabic uses of بين as a noun without ما, including Qur'anic examples and poetry.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#8/r2.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: " وكذلك نقرؤها بالرفع لأنا قد وجدنا العرب تجعل " بين " اسما

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#8/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#8/r3.speaker: الكسائي
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#8/r3.claim: Al-Kisai reads بين accusatively, following the wording of Abdullah's reading لقد تقطع ما بينكم.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#8/r3.anchor: وقرأها الكسائي نصبا، وكان يعتبرها بحرف عبد الله " لقد تقطع ما بينكم "

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#8/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#8/r4.speaker: الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#8/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj prefers the nominative but allows the accusative; both mean that the association between them was severed.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#8/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج: " والرفع أجود والنصب جائز، والمعنى: لقد تقطع ما كان من الشركة بينكم

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#8/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#8/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#8/r5.claim: A third explanation paraphrases the meaning as the group being scattered, but the author says this does not provide a grammatical parse.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#8/r5.anchor: الثالث: أن هذا كلام محمول على معناه إذ المعنى: لقد تفرق جمعكم وتشتت

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#9/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#9/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#9/r1.claim: ما in ما كنتم may be a relative noun, an indefinite noun described by a clause, or a masdariyya particle.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#9/r1.anchor: " ما " يجوز أن تكون موصولة اسمية أو نكرة موصوفة

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#9/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#9/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#9/r2.claim: If ما is relative or indefinite, its antecedent and both objects of تزعمون are elided for concision, understood as you deem them partners or intercessors.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#9/r2.anchor: والتقدير: تزعمونهم شركاء أو شفعاء، فالعائد

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#9/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#9/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#9/r3.claim: If ما is masdariyya, there is no antecedent to recover, but the second object of تزعمون must still be supplied.
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#9/r3.anchor: إن قلنا إنها مصدرية، لأن المصدرية لا تحتاج إلى عائد بخلاف غيرها

SAMIN-DURR:6:94#9/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#9/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:94#9/r4.claim: The cited poem illustrates omission of the second object after تحسب: its sense is you deem their love a disgrace to me.

ZAJJAJ:v2p273/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p273/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p273/r1.claim: فرادى means each person is alone, separated from a partner in error and a close companion.
ZAJJAJ:v2p273/r1.anchor: (فرادى) فكل واحد منفرد من شريكه في الغي وشقيقه.

ZAJJAJ:v2p273/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p273/r2.speaker: جاء في التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v2p273/r2.claim: A reported gloss says people will arrive naked and uncircumcised; الغرل are the uncircumcised.
ZAJJAJ:v2p273/r2.anchor: جاء في التفسير: عراة غرلا، والغرل هم الغلف.

ZAJJAJ:v2p273/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p273/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p273/r3.claim: The language also allows the sense that resurrection is like their first creation.
ZAJJAJ:v2p273/r3.anchor: كما بدأناكم أول مرة، أي كان بعثكم كخلقكم.

ZAJJAJ:v2p273/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p273/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p273/r4.claim: The nominative reading is better and means that the bond between them has been severed; accusative is also allowed for the partnership that had linked them.
ZAJJAJ:v2p273/r4.anchor: الرفع أجود، ومعناه لقد تقطع وصلكم. والنصب جائز. المعنى: لقد تقطع ماكنتم فيه من الشركة بينكم.

ASAD-NOTES:6:94#n78/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:94#n78/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:6:94#n78/r1.claim: The alleged partners are supposed to share in God's divinity by protecting or helping those who invoke them; Asad refers to 6:22, note 15.
ASAD-NOTES:6:94#n78/r1.anchor: whom you supposed to be [God's] partners with regard to you - i.e., being able, in result of their alleged "share in God's divinity", to protect or help you

ASAD-NOTES:6:94#n79/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:94#n79/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:6:94#n79/r1.claim: The things that have vanished are the imagined intercessors or mediators between humanity and God.
ASAD-NOTES:6:94#n79/r1.anchor: all that you were wont to assert [or "to suppose"] has gone away from you" - i.e., all the imaginary intercessors or mediators between man and God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p78/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p78/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p78/.claim: The passage turns from miscreants among the People of the Book to the idolaters of Makkah and briefly recalls their nonsensical remarks.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p78/.anchor: After the miscreants among the People of the Book, attention is now directed to the Idolaters of Makah.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p80/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p80/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p80/.claim: The section ending at 6:94 concludes its monotheism discussion; the next section argues for monotheism from the world around us, also supporting prophethood and the hereafter, and recalls Abraham's method of reflection.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p80/.anchor: The above section of verses concluded on the topic of monotheism.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p80/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p80/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p80/.claim: Across the sūra, monotheism, the hereafter, and prophethood recur; objections and audience responses prompt refutation, explanation, assurance, or directives while the central thread remains intact.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p80/.anchor: the content of the sūrah progresses in this same way: central theme, monotheism, hereafter and prophethood are repeatedly discussed in different styles.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p80/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p80/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p80/.claim: The address becomes direct, as if Judgment Day has arrived, making the terrifying fate described earlier vivid before the audience.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p80/.anchor: has become direct so that the horrific nature of the fate referred to in

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p80/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p80/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p80/.claim: They come before God alone, without the wealth, supporters, or intercessors they expected to accompany them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p80/.anchor: They will become before God without any wealth or supporters or intercessors which they thought would be there to help them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p80/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p80/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p80/.claim: Humans begin without abilities; God develops them and grants resources to test gratitude or arrogance, then they return empty-handed, taking none of it along.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p80/.anchor: The purpose is to see whether he becomes grateful to God or shows arrogance. Then comes a day when he returns to God empty handed.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p80/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p80/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p80/.claim: The subject of “the ties between you have been cut” is suppressed; the implied subject is the cord, referring to the absent intercessors.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p80/.anchor: the fā‘il in them has been suppressed. The actual construction is to the effect:

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p356#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p356#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير، وأبو عمرو، وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر، وابن عامر، وحمزة
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p356#2/r1.claim: These readers pronounce baynakum in لقد تقطع بينكم with nominative inflection.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p356#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم. في رواية أبي بكر، وابن عامر وحمزة: لقد تقطع بينكم رفعا.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p356#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p356#2/r2.speaker: نافع والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p356#2/r2.claim: Nafi, al-Kisaʾi, and Hafs from Asim read baynakum in the accusative.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p356#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ نافع والكسائي بينكم نصبا. وكذلك روى حفص عن عاصم بالنصب أيضا .

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p356#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p356#2/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p356#2/r3.claim: Al-Farisi derives al-bayn from bāna, meaning to part or separate, and cites poetry using it for separation.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p356#2/r3.anchor: البين مصدر بان يبين إذا فارق، قال : بان الخليط برامتين فودعوا ... أو كلما ظعنوا لبين تجزع

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p356#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p356#2/r4.speaker: أبو زيد
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p356#2/r4.claim: Abu Zayd uses bāna/bayn for a departing group and also for the limit reached by sight, such as a wall.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p356#2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو زيد: بان الحي بينونة وبينا

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p356#2/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p356#2/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p356#2/r5.claim: In the nominative reading, bayn is a former adverb used as a noun and can therefore serve as the subject of taqaṭṭaʿa.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p356#2/r5.anchor: فالمرفوع في قراءة من قرأ لقد تقطع بينكم هو الذي كان ظرفا ثم استعمل اسما.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p356#2/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p356#2/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p356#2/r6.claim: Treating the nominative as the verbal noun ‘separation’ would mean ‘your separation was cut,’ contrary to the intended severing of the bond among them.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p356#2/r6.anchor: فلا يجوز أن يكون هذا القسم، لأن التقدير يصير: لقد تقطع افتراقكم. وهذا، مع بعده عن القصد، خلاف المعنى المراد، ألا ترى أن المراد: لقد تقطع وصلكم

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p358/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p358/r1.speaker: الحديث
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p358/r1.claim: A hadith cited as lexical evidence says that what separates from a living creature is carrion.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p358/r1.anchor: وفي الحديث «ما بان من الحي فهو ميتة».

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p358/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p358/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p358/r2.claim: Because bayn is used between two closely connected parties, it can come to mean their bond; thus ‘your bayn was severed’ means your bond was cut.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p358/r2.anchor: قيل: إنه لما استعمل مع الشيئين المتلابسين في نحو: بيني وبينه شركة، وبيني وبينه رحم وصداقة، صارت لاستعمالها في هذه المواضع بمنزلة الوصلة

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p358/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p358/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p358/r3.claim: Wasṭ, like bayn, normally functions as an adverb but is also used as a noun, as shown in poetry and in Sibawayh’s example ‘red between the eyes.’
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p358/r3.anchor: ومثل بين في أنه يجري في الكلام ظرفا، ثم يستعمل اسما: «وسط» الساكن العين، ألا ترى أنك تقول: جلست وسط القوم

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p358/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p358/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p358/r4.claim: One accusative analysis supplies an omitted subject, al-waṣl, inferred from the preceding mention of alleged partners and their division; contextual implication can stand for prior mention.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p358/r4.anchor: أحدهما: أنه أضمر الفاعل في الفعل ودل عليه مما تقدم في قوله: وما نرى معكم شفعاءكم الذين زعمتم أنهم فيكم شركاء

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p358/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p358/r5.speaker: أبو الحسن
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p358/r5.claim: Abu al-Hasan treats accusative bayn as having the nominative reading’s sense while retaining its usual adverbial accusative form, as in 60:3 and 72:11.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p358/r5.anchor: والمذهب الآخر: انتصاب البين في قوله: لقد تقطع بينكم على شيء يقوله أبو الحسن،

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p145#2/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p145#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p145#2/r1.claim: With ḍamma, bayn is a nominative noun meaning your bond or connection, not an adverb; a line of verse supports this nominal use.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p145#2/r1.anchor: فالحجة لمن قرأ بالضم أنه جعله اسما

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p145#2/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p145#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p145#2/r2.claim: With fatḥa, bayn is an adverb meaning the space between two endpoints; ʿAbd Allāh's “what was between you” supports it, as do uses of dun and wasat as nouns or adverbs.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p145#2/r2.anchor: والحجة لمن قرأ بالفتح أنه جعله ظرفا ومعناه الفضاء بين الغايتين ودليله قراءة عبد الله لقد تقطع ما بينكم

NASHR:v1p451/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p451/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p451/r1.claim: One account preserves the second of two alifs and deletes the first: the first is extra, both are silent, and the second has already undergone substitution, so it should not also be deleted.
NASHR:v1p451/r1.anchor: أحدها أن الأولى زائدة، والثانية أصلية، والزائد أولى بالحذف، والأصلي أولى بالثبوت

NASHR:v1p451/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p451/r2.speaker: غيره
NASHR:v1p451/r2.claim: The opposing account preserves the first alif and deletes the second because it conveys meaning, is word-final, is deleted in connected speech, and causes the disliked identical sequence.
NASHR:v1p451/r2.anchor: وذهب غيره إلى أن الثانية هي الأولى، وأن الثانية هي المحذوفة، واستدلوا بخمسة أوجه

NASHR:v1p451/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p451/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p451/r3.claim: Replies hold that an added letter is preferentially deleted only when it is mere expansion, that the change for meeting two silent letters is common, and that phonetic alteration and orthographic deletion occur in separate domains.
NASHR:v1p451/r3.anchor: وأجابوا عن الأولى بأن الزائد إنما يكون أولى بالحذف من الأصلي إذا كانت الزيادة لمجرد التوسع

NASHR:v1p451/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p451/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p451/r4.claim: Eight words with final hamza after alif are written with the hamza on waw without disagreement; the listed examples include شركاء in al-Anʿām, نشاء in Hūd, and دعاء in Ghāfir.
NASHR:v1p451/r4.anchor: فالمضمومة منها ثمان كلمات كتبت الهمزة فيها واوا بلا خلاف، وهي (شركاء) في الأنعام

NASHR:v1p474/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p474/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p474/r2.claim: When the final hamza is kasra or damma, the same five forms apply if no written hamza sign is present; non-Hijazi readers add four forms, bringing the total to nine.
NASHR:v1p474/r2.anchor: فإن رسم للهمز فيه صورة جاز في المكسور منه نحو (وإيتاي ذي القربى، ومن آناي الليل)

NASHR:v1p474/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p474/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p474/r3.claim: The combinations multiply to eighteen for وايتاي and twenty-seven for ومن آناي when initial hamza treatment, pause, and transfer are counted; a damma case adds three rounded-waw options for a total of twelve.
NASHR:v1p474/r3.anchor: فيجيء معه المد والقصر، وفيه نظر فيصير خمسة، وتجيء هذه الخمسة بلا نظر

NASHR:v2p259/r12.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p259/r12.speaker: المدنيان والكسائي وحفص
NASHR:v2p259/r12.claim: The two Medinan readers, al-Kisāʾī, and Hafs read baynakum in the accusative form.
NASHR:v2p259/r12.anchor: فقرأ المدنيان، والكسائي وحفص بنصب النون

NASHR:v2p259/r13.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p259/r13.speaker: الباقون
NASHR:v2p259/r13.claim: The remaining readers read baynakum in the nominative form.
NASHR:v2p259/r13.anchor: وقرأ الباقون برفعها، وتقدم اختلافهم في " الميت " عند إنما حرم عليكم الميتة في البقرة

QIRAAT-ER:6:94:30#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:6:94:30#1/r1.speaker: CE
QIRAAT-ER:6:94:30#1/r1.claim: The nominative baynukum makes the relation itself the subject of taqaṭṭaʿa, as though the bond between them were a substantive thing that was severed.
QIRAAT-ER:6:94:30#1/r1.anchor: Nominative reading — baynukum becomes the subject of taqaṭṭaʿa: ""your between-ness has been severed""

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p214/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p214/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p214/r1.claim: Qatāda explains that what has been severed is the bond that once existed between you.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p214/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ لقد تقطع بينكم ﴾ قال ما كان بينكم من الوصل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r7.speaker: النضر بن الحارث
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r7.claim: Ikrima reports al-Nadr's claim that al-Lat and al-Uzza would intercede, followed by the revelation of this passage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r7.anchor: قال عكرمة قال النضر بن الحارث: سوف تشفع في اللات والعزى فنزلت: ولما قال اليوم تجزون عذاب الهون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r8.claim: The verse confronts them with arriving alone at resurrection, without worldly wealth or intercessors to rely on; the speech may be by the angels assigned to punish them or by God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r8.anchor: وقفهم على أنهم يقدمون يوم القيامة منفردين لا ناظر لهم محتاجين إليه بعد أن كانوا ذوي خول وشفعاء في الدنيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r9.claim: The alternative that God speaks to them presupposes that God addresses unbelievers, as supported by the verses about questioning those sent and questioning them all.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r9.anchor: وقيل: هو كلام الله لهم وهذا مبني على أن الله تعالى يكلم الكفار، وهو ظاهر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r10.claim: The past tense may be used for a future event, or the statement may recount what they actually say while standing for judgment and reckoning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r10.anchor: وجئتمونا من الماضي الذي أريد به المستقبل، وقيل: هو ماض على حقيقته محكي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that they come individually, separated from family, wealth, and children.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فرادى من الأهل والمال والولد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r12.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r12.claim: Al-Hasan says each person comes alone, with no helpers or intercessors.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r12.anchor: وقال الحسن: كل واحد على حدته بلا أعوان ولا شفعاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r13.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r13.claim: Muqatil says they bring none of the worldly things in which they took pride.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r13.anchor: وقال مقاتل: ليس معكم شيء من الدنيا تفتخرون به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r14.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r14.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains the word as each person separated from his partner and intercessor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r14.anchor: وقال الزجاج: كل واحد مفرد عن شريكه وشفيعه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r15.speaker: ابن كيسان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r15.claim: Ibn Kaysan says they come separated from the object they worshipped.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r15.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان: فرادى من المعبود

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r16.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r16.claim: Another explanation is that they are restored without any helper or defender.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r16.anchor: وقيل: أعدناكم بلا معين ولا ناصر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r17.claim: One reading has فراد without declension; Isa ibn Umar and Abu Haywa read فرادا with tanwin; Abu Amr and Nafi, in Kharija's report, read فردى like سكرى, feminine for the collective.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r17.anchor: وقرئ فراد غير مصروف، وقرأ عيسى بن عمر وأبو حيوة فرادا بالتنوين وأبو عمرو ونافع في حكاية خارجة عنهما فردى مثل سكرى كقوله: وترى الناس سكارى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r18.claim: The kāf in كما is accusative, either as an appositive to فرادى or an adjective to an omitted verbal noun, comparing their coming with their original creation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r18.anchor: والكاف في كما في موضع نصب، قيل: بدل من فرادى، وقيل: نعت لمصدر محذوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r19.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r19.claim: The comparison evokes their first creation without property, children, or attendants; some say naked and uncircumcised, and the description as they were born can include both.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r19.anchor: لأن الإنسان يخلق أقشر لا مال له ولا ولد ولا حشم، وقيل: عراة غرلا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r20.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r20.claim: أول مرة is an adverb of time; it cannot mean the first act of God's creation because the subsequent event is resurrection, not a second creation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p586/r20.anchor: وانتصب أول مرة على الظرف أي أول زمان ولا يتقدر أول خلق الله لأن أول خلق يستدعي خلقا ثانيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r1.claim: What God bestowed in worldly life is now useless; they neither carried away a tiny amount nor sent it ahead for themselves.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r1.anchor: ما تفضلنا به عليكم في الدنيا لم ينفعكم ولم تحتملوا منه نقيرا ولا قدمتموه لأنفسكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r2.claim: Behind your backs points to worldly possessions left intact when they depart.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r2.anchor: وأشار بقوله: وراء ظهوركم إلى الدنيا لأنهم يتركون ما خولوه موجودا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r3.claim: The challenge rebukes them for worshipping and magnifying idols that are absent as intercessors.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r3.anchor: وقفهم على الخطأ في عبادتهم الأصنام وتعظيمها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r4.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r4.claim: Muqatil says they believed angels would intercede and claimed they worshipped them only to bring them nearer to God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل: كانوا يعتقدون شفاعة الملائكة ويقولون: ما نعبدهم إلا ليقربونا إلى الله زلفى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r5.claim: فيكم modifies شركاء; by worshipping the idols as gods, they made them partners over themselves in their service and enslavement.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r5.anchor: وفيكم متعلق بشركاء والمعنى في استعبادكم لأنهم حين دعوهم آلهة وعبدوها فقد جعلوا لله شركاء فيهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r6.claim: Another possible sense is that they made the idols partners with God as intercessors or as partners in saving them from punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r6.anchor: وقيل: جعلوهم شركاء لله باعتبار أنهم يشفعون فيهم عنده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r7.claim: فيكم may mean in your estimation or among you.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r8.speaker: ابن قتيبة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r8.claim: Ibn Qutayba takes the claim to mean that the idols were partners with God in creating the people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r8.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة إنهم لي في خلقكم شركاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r9.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r9.claim: Another explanation is that the supposed partners would bear some of the punishment for them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r9.anchor: وقيل: متحملون عنكم نصيبا من العذاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r10.claim: Most of the seven readers have بينكم in the nominative; analyses take the adverb as a noun with the verb attached to it, or take بين to mean bond or separation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r10.anchor: قرأ جمهور السبعة بينكم بالرفع على أنه اتسع في الظرف وأسند الفعل إليه فصار اسما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r11.speaker: أبو الفتح والزهراوي والمهدوي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r11.claim: Abu al-Fath, al-Zahrawi, and al-Mahdawi explain nominative بينكم as connection, yielding the sense that your bond has been severed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r11.anchor: أو على أنه أريد بالبين الوصل أي لقد تقطع وصلكم قاله أبو الفتح والزهراوي والمهدوي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r12.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r12.claim: Ibn Atiyya rejects the sense of بين as connection, saying it is unattested in Arab usage and was inferred from this verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r12.anchor: وقطع فيه ابن عطية وزعم أنه لم يسمع من العرب البين بمعنى الوصل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r13.claim: Another interpretation takes بين as separation: the distance between them was cut through its great length, a figurative expression.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r13.anchor: أو على أنه أريد بالبين الافتراق وذلك مجاز عن الأمر البعيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r14.speaker: نافع والكسائي وحفص
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r14.claim: Nafi, al-Kisaʾi, and Hafs read بينكم with a fatḥa; al-Akhfash parses it as the subject, while others parse it adverbially with التقطع as subject.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p587/r14.anchor: وقرأ نافع والكسائي وحفص بينكم بفتح النون وخرجه الأخفش على أنه فاعل ولكنه مبني على الفتح

ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r1.claim: They arrive alone, separated either from the helpers and idols they claimed would intercede or from the wealth, children, and other worldly things they preferred.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r1.anchor: عن الاعوان والأوثان التي زعمتم أنها شفعاؤكم أو عن الأموال والأولاد

ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r2.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r2.claim: Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and others report from ʿIkrima that al-Nadr ibn al-Harith said al-Lat and al-ʿUzza would intercede for him, and the verse was revealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة قال : قال النضر بن الحرث سوف تشفع لي اللات والعزى فنزلت

ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r3.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r3.claim: Some verifiers read the sentence as a fresh divine statement; this does not conflict with the denial that God speaks to them, since that denies beneficial speech or signals anger.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r3.anchor: والجملة على ماذهب اليه بعض المحققين مستأنفة من كلامه تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r4.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r4.claim: An alternative links the sentence to the angels’ words ordering the sinners out; the Imam considers it stronger, but al-Alusi calls it far-fetched.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r4.anchor: من جملة كلامهم وفيه بعد وإن ظنه الأمام أولى وأقوى

ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r5.claim: Furāda is an accusative circumstantial expression from the subject, an irregular plural of fard, with the feminine alif.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r5.anchor: على الحال من ضمير الفاعل وهو جمع فرد على خلاف القياس

ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r6.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r6.claim: Aisha worries that men and women will be resurrected together and see one another naked; the Prophet replies each will be absorbed in their own affair and men and women will not look at each other. Al-Hakim authenticated the report.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r6.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي حاتم والحاكم وصححه عن عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها أنها قرأت هذه الآية فقالت

ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r7.claim: Arabic usage gives several forms of furād and related expressions meaning one by one; the singular appears as fard, furd, farīd, or fardān, while fard is not used in this sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r7.anchor: أي واحدا بعد واحد والواحد فرد وفرد وفريد وفردان

ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r8.claim: Readings include furādā with a rounded first vowel and firād like aḥād or rubāʿ as an indeclinable adjective; al-Farra and others say this pattern is not restricted to numerals, and firda is feminine of fardān.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r8.anchor: وقريء ( فرادا ) كرخال المضموم الراء وفراد كاحاد ورباع

ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r9.claim: The phrase may be an all-of-it substitute for furādā; kāf is a noun meaning ‘like’; it can instead be a second or coordinated circumstantial, or describe the manner of coming.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r9.anchor: بدل من فرادى بدل كل لأن المراد المشابهة فى الانفراد المذكور والكاف اسم بمعنى مثل

ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r10.claim: The comparison may concern the initial creation: people are like they were at birth, barefoot, naked, uncircumcised, and without speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p224#2/r10.anchor: مشبهين ابتداء خلقكم بمعنى شبيهة حالكم حال ابتداء خلقكم حفاة عراة غرلا بهما

ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r1.claim: What God granted in the world means wealth and servants; the phrasing rebukes people for letting these occupy them at the expense of the afterlife.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r1.anchor: أي ما أعطيناكم في الدنيا من المال والخدم وهو متضمن للتوبيخ

ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r2.claim: They left worldly provisions behind and had sent nothing ahead for themselves.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r2.anchor: وراء ظهوركم ما قدمتم منه شيئا لأنفسكم

ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r3.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says Adam’s child is brought on Judgment Day, God asks where his gathered wealth is, and he says he left it intact; asked what he sent ahead, he sees that he sent nothing and recites the verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r3.anchor: عن الحسن قال : يؤتى بان آدم يوم القيامة كأنه بذخ

ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r4.claim: The clause is analyzed either as independent or as circumstantial with an implied qad.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r4.anchor: والجملة قيل مستأنفة أو حال بتقدير قد

ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r5.claim: Abu al-Baqa takes ‘we see’ as a portrayal of the present scene; maʿakum attaches to the verb, not as a circumstance from shufaʿāʾ or a second object, and the seeing is visual.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r5.anchor: أي نبصر وهو على ما نص عليه أبو البقاء حكاية حال

ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r6.claim: The intercessors are called ‘yours’ according to the addressees’ claim, as the description ‘whom you claimed’ makes explicit.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r6.anchor: وإضافة الشفعاء إلى ضمير المخاطبين باعتبار الزعم

ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r7.claim: The alleged partners were supposed to share God’s lordship over the people and their entitlement to worship.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r7.anchor: أي شركاء لله تعالى في ربوبيتكم واستحقاق عبادتكم

ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r8.claim: Zaʿm explicitly denotes a false claim here, though it can also be used of truth, as indicated earlier and in the cited verse of poetry.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r8.anchor: والزعم هنا نص في الباطل وجاء استعماله في الحق كما تقدمت الاشارة اليه

ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r9.speaker: عاصم والكسائي وحفص
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r9.claim: ʿAsim, al-Kisaʾi, and Hafs from ʿAsim read bayn with the accusative; one parsing supplies an understood subject such as affair or connection, while Abu Hayyan rejects a verbal-noun subject because subject and predicate would not differ.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r9.anchor: قراءة عاصم والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم واختلف في تخريج ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r10.claim: The proposed objection to a verbal-noun subject is answered by the attested phrase badaʾa badaʾ and by the similar parsing of the cited Quranic expression.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r10.anchor: ورد بأنه سمع بدا بداء وقد قدروا

ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r11.speaker: السفاقسى
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r11.claim: Al-Safaqisi says advocates of the verbal-noun subject mean that severance occurred; the definite verbal noun and the indefinite verb remain distinct even if the action is the same.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225/r11.anchor: إن من جعل الفاعل ضمير المصدر

ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r1.claim: If the subject is the verbal noun itself, the reading needs figurative interpretation: severing severance would imply renewed connection, contrary to the intended sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r1.anchor: أن القول بالتأويل متعين على هذا التقدير لأنه إذا تقطع التقطع حصل الوصل وهو ضد المقصود

ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r2.speaker: الأخفش
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash treats bayn as the subject while retaining its accusative by analogy with its most common case; another view says it is indeclinable because annexed to an indeclinable word.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r2.anchor: إن بين هو الفاعل وبقي على حاله منصوبا حملا له على أغلب أحواله

ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r3.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan prefers a competition construction: the two verbs govern the claimed objects, the later verb ḍalla takes the object and a pronoun is understood with taqaṭṭaʿ; the idols are meant, with no remaining connection between worshippers and claimed partners.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r3.anchor: واختار أبو حيان أن الكلام من باب التنازع

ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r4.claim: The other seven readers use the nominative, making bayn the subject; it means connection here, so ties are severed and the group is dispersed.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r4.anchor: بالرفع على الفاعلية وهو من الأضداد كالقرء يستعمل في الوصل والفصل

ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya objects that Arabic usage does not attest bayn meaning connection, and says this sense is inferred from this verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r5.anchor: وطعن ابن عطية فى هدا بأنه لم يسمع من العرب أن البين يمعنى الوصل

ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r6.claim: Al-Alusi answers that connection is a valid metaphor needing no attestation, supported by phrases such as ‘between us is kinship’ and by Abu ʿAmr, Abu ʿUbayda, Ibn Jinni, and al-Zajjaj, who record the sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r6.anchor: معنى مجازي ولا يتوقف على السماع

ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r7.claim: On the connection reading bayn is a verbal noun, though another analysis leaves it an adverb used as a subject by syntactic extension.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r7.anchor: وعليه فيكون مصدرا لا ظرفا وقيل إن بين هنا ظرف لكنه أسند إليه الفعل على سبيل الاتساع

ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r8.speaker: عبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r8.claim: ʿAbd Allah reads the phrase with the relative or descriptive ma attached to taqaṭṭaʿ.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p225#2/r9.claim: Ḍalla means the claimed objects vanished, were lost, or became null; the claims may have concerned intercession, partnership with God, or denial of resurrection and requital.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r1.claim: On Resurrection the disbelievers come one by one, without wealth, spouse, children, or servants.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r1.anchor: هذا خبر من الله أنه يقول للكفار يوم القيامة: ولقد جئتمونا فرادى وحدانا، لا مال معكم ولا زوج ولا ولد ولا خدم،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r2.claim: فرادى is the plural of فردان, as سكران becomes سكارى and كسلان becomes كسالى.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r2.anchor: وفرادى جمع فردان، مثل سكران وسكارى، وكسلان وكسالى،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r3.speaker: الأعرج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r3.claim: Al-Aʿraj reads فردى without the alif, like سكرى.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r3.anchor: وقرأ الأعرج فردى بغير ألف مثل سكرى،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r4.claim: They return as first created: naked, barefoot, and uncircumcised.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r4.anchor: {كما خلقناكم أول مرة} عراة حفاة غرلا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r5.claim: ما خولناكم means what God bestowed: wealth, children, servants; وراء ظهوركم means left behind in worldly life.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r5.anchor: {وتركتم} خلفتم {ما خولناكم} أعطيناكم من الأموال والأولاد والخدم، {وراء ظهوركم} خلف ظهوركم في الدنيا،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r6.claim: The supposed intercessors are the idols the polytheists worshipped as partners with God and advocates for them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r6.anchor: {وما نرى معكم شفعاءكم الذين زعمتم أنهم فيكم شركاء} وذلك أن المشركين زعموا أنهم يعبدون الأصنام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r7.speaker: أهل المدينة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r7.claim: The Medinese, al-Kisaʾi, and Hafs from Asim read بينكم with the nūn in the accusative.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r7.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم بنصب النون، أي: لقد تقطع ما بينكم من الوصل،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r8.claim: With the accusative reading, the connection between them, or their affair, has been cut off.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r8.anchor: أي: لقد تقطع ما بينكم من الوصل، أو تقطع الأمر بينكم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r9.speaker: الآخرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r9.claim: Other readers use the nominative nūn and understand the connection between them as severed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r9.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون "بينكم" برفع النون، أي: لقد تقطع [وصلكم]

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r10.claim: The severing is compared to the connections being cut in 2:166.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r11.claim: بين has two opposite senses: connection and separation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r11.anchor: والبين من الأضداد يكون وصلا ويكون هجرا،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p169#3/r12.claim: The objects of their claims will be absent and lost to them.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r1.claim: They come before God for reckoning and recompense.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r1.anchor: للحساب والجزاء. { فرادى } منفردين عن الأموال والأولاد

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r2.claim: They arrive alone, separated from possessions, children, and worldly attachments, or from the helpers and idols they claimed would intercede.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r2.anchor: منفردين عن الأموال والأولاد وسائر ما آثرتموه من الدنيا

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r3.claim: Furādā is a plural of fard, with the final alif marking the feminine plural form.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r3.anchor: وهو جمع فرد والألف للتأنيث ككسالى

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r4.claim: Variants include furād, compared to rikhāl or thulāth, and fardā, compared to sukrā.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r5.claim: The comparison may be an appositive, a second circumstantial clause, a circumstance of furādā, or an adjective describing the manner of coming.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r5.anchor: على الهيئة التي ولدتم عليها في الانفراد، أو حال ثانية

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r6.claim: One explanation compares their arrival with first creation: barefoot, unclothed, uncircumcised, and solitary.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r6.anchor: ابتداء خلقكم عراة حفاة غرلا بهما

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r7.claim: What God bestowed in worldly life distracted them from the afterlife, but they left it behind and carried away nothing, not even a tiny amount.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r7.anchor: ما تفضلنا به عليكم في الدنيا فشغلتم به عن الآخرة

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r8.claim: The alleged partners were claimed to share God’s lordship over them and their entitlement to worship.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r8.anchor: شفعاءكم الذين زعمتم أنهم فيكم شركاء

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r9.claim: The phrase means their bond has been severed and their gathering scattered; bayn can mean connection or separation.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r10.claim: Alternatively, bayn is an adverb made subject to the verb by extension, meaning severance occurred among them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r10.anchor: وقيل هو ظرف أسند إليه الفعل اتساعا

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r11.speaker: نافع والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r11.claim: They read baynakum in the accusative with an omitted agent inferred from what precedes; another attested form supplies mā before baynakum.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r11.anchor: قراءة نافع والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم بالنصب

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r12.claim: Their claim was either that idols would intercede for them or that there would be no resurrection and recompense.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:94/r12.anchor: ما كنتم تزعمون } أنها شفعاؤكم أو أن لا بعث ولا جزاء

BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r1.claim: The context answers deniers who thought the dead neither sensed anything nor understood speech: angels seize them, none can prevent it, and the angels at the surah’s beginning signal a final judgment without delay.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r1.anchor: الذين أخبرناكم أول السورة أنهم إذا أبصروا

BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r2.claim: Their arrival before God displays His overwhelming majesty, through the death that decisively demonstrates His complete knowledge and power.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r2.anchor: ملا لنا من العظمة بالموت الذي هو دال على شمول علمنا وتمام قدرتنا قطعا

BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r3.claim: They come separately, no one accompanying another, and stripped of every attachment that had kept them from following the messengers.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r4.claim: They return as isolated, weak, and poor as at their first creation, exposing the emptiness of the worldly gathering in which they took pride.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r4.anchor: فأين جمعكم الذي كنتم به تستكبرون

BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r5.claim: What God granted was wealth and the ability to manage it as a blessing for seeking His pleasure; they instead treated it as intrinsically theirs and turned from Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r5.anchor: ملكناكم من المال ومكناكم من إصلاحه نعمة عليكم لتتوصلوا به إلى رضانا

BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r6.claim: They left their wealth behind, so it cannot help them or preserve the status they once claimed through it.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r6.anchor: فما أغنى عنكم ما كنتم منه تستكبرون

BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r7.claim: They hoped their idols would intercede, mockingly or in this world or—if resurrection is granted—in the next; God taunts them by demanding to see the absent intercessors.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r8.claim: They falsely claimed idols shared God’s authority over them, worshipping the idols in ease and invoking them in hardship; no screen can conceal them from God.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r8.anchor: أن لهم فيكم نصيبا مع الله حتى كنتم تعبدونهم في وقت الرخاء وتدعونه في وقت الشدة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r9.claim: The phrase introduces the terrified unbelievers’ bewildered and helpless response, marked by confusion, shock, and humiliation.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p675/r9.anchor: دل على بهتهم في جواب هذا الكلام الهائل المرعب حيرة وعجزا ودهشا وذلا

BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r1.claim: ‘Between you’ usually signals presence or nearness; its severance here is so complete that even the thought of former connection vanishes, leaving no path of contact.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r1.anchor: ذكر البين في شيء يدل على قربه في الجملة وحضوره ولو في الذهن

BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r2.speaker: نافع والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r2.claim: The majority read the word in the nominative, while Nāfiʿ, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read it in the accusative as an adverbial expression; the meaning remains severed connection.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r2.anchor: قراءة نافع والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم بالنصب

BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r3.claim: The connection’s end stems from the disappearance of what they relied on; everything they falsely claimed has gone and become void.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p676/r3.anchor: وهو زوال المستند الذي كانوا يستندون إليه

DURR-FULL:v3p322/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p322/r6.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v3p322/r6.claim: Ikrima reports that al-Nadr ibn al-Harith claimed al-Lat and al-Uzza would intercede for him, and this verse was revealed in response.
DURR-FULL:v3p322/r6.anchor: عن عكرمة قال: قال النضر بن الحارث: سوف تشفع لي اللات والعزى

DURR-FULL:v3p322/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p322/r7.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v3p322/r7.claim: Aisha worried that men and women would see one another naked at the Resurrection; the Prophet replied that each would be too occupied with personal concerns to look.
DURR-FULL:v3p322/r7.anchor: عن عائشة أنها قرأت قول الله {ولقد جئتمونا فرادى كما خلقناكم أول مرة}

DURR-FULL:v3p322/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p322/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v3p322/r8.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says they come as on the day they were born, with all that had been lost since birth restored to them.
DURR-FULL:v3p322/r8.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله {ولقد جئتمونا فرادى كما خلقناكم أول مرة}

DURR-FULL:v3p323/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p323/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p323/r1.claim: The Prophet says people will be gathered barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised.
DURR-FULL:v3p323/r1.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله رضي الله عنه سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

DURR-FULL:v3p323/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p323/r2.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v3p323/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says what God bestowed is wealth and servants, which people left behind in worldly life.
DURR-FULL:v3p323/r2.anchor: عن السدي رضي الله عنه في قوله {وتركتم ما خولناكم} قال: من المال والخدم

DURR-FULL:v3p323/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p323/r3.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v3p323/r3.claim: Hasan describes God asking the resurrected person where his amassed wealth is; he says he left it abundant, but has advanced nothing for himself, then Hasan recites the verse.
DURR-FULL:v3p323/r3.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه قال: يؤتى بابن آدم يوم القيامة كأنه بذخ

DURR-FULL:v3p323/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p323/r4.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر
DURR-FULL:v3p323/r4.claim: Yahya ibn Ya'mar judged the disputed reading by reading the word between as nominative.
DURR-FULL:v3p323/r4.anchor: فدخل يحيى بن يعمر فسألوه فقال: بينكم بالرفع

DURR-FULL:v3p323/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p323/r5.speaker: الأعرج
DURR-FULL:v3p323/r5.claim: Al-Araj read بينكم in the nominative, taking the bond between them as what was severed.
DURR-FULL:v3p323/r5.anchor: عن الأعرج أنه قرأ (لقد تقطع بينكم) بالرفع يعني وصلكم

DURR-FULL:v3p323/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p323/r6.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v3p323/r6.claim: Hasan read بينكم in the accusative, meaning the ties of connection they had in worldly life.
DURR-FULL:v3p323/r6.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه أنه قرأ (لقد تقطع بينكم) بالنصب

DURR-FULL:v3p323/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p323/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v3p323/r7.claim: Qatada glosses the severed connection as whatever bonds had existed between them.
DURR-FULL:v3p323/r7.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه (لقد تقطع بينكم) قال: ما كان بينهم من الوصل

DURR-FULL:v3p323/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p323/r8.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v3p323/r8.claim: Ikrima reports that Umar married Umm Kulthum, daughter of Ali, to establish kinship with the Prophet, citing the saying that every lineage and bond ends at the Resurrection except the Prophet’s.
DURR-FULL:v3p323/r8.anchor: عن عكرمة قال: لما تزوج عمر رضي الله عنه أم كلثوم رضي الله عنها بنت علي

DURR-FULL:v3p323/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p323/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p323/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says the severed ties and lost claims refer to kinship and dwellings.
DURR-FULL:v3p323/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {لقد تقطع بينكم وضل عنكم ما كنتم تزعمون}

DURR-FULL:v3p324/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r1.claim: Mujahid explains the severed connection as the bonds and mutual association people had in worldly life.
DURR-FULL:v3p324/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {لقد تقطع بينكم} قال: تواصلكم في الدنيا

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r1.speaker: عائشة
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r1.claim: Aisha worries that men and women will be resurrected together and see one another's nakedness.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r1.anchor: فقالت عائشة : يا رسول الله ، واسواناه ! ان الرجال والنساء سيحشرون جميعا ينظر بعضهم إلى سواة بعض

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r2.claim: The Prophet answers that each person will be absorbed in his own affair; men and women will not look at one another.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r2.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : لكل امرئ منهم يومئذ شان يغنيه لا ينظر الرجال إلى النساء

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r3.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says people return as on the day they were born, with whatever had been removed from them since birth restored.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير انه تلا هذه الاية : ولقد جئتمونا فرادى كما خلقناكم اول مرة قال : كيوم ولد يرد عليه كل شيء نقص منه من يوم ولد

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan describes the resurrected person as brought like a lamb; God asks what he amassed and what he sent ahead, and he finds that he sent nothing.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r4.anchor: عن الحسن قال يؤتى بابن ادم يوم القيامة كانه بذج فيقول له تبارك وتعالى اين ما جمعت

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r5.claim: Al-Suddī says what God bestowed refers to wealth and servants.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r5.anchor: عن السدى : قوله : وتركتم ما خولناكم من المال والخدم

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r6.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r6.claim: Al-Suddī says “behind your backs” means in the worldly life.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r6.anchor: وبه عن السدى : قوله : وراء ظهوركم قال : في الدنيا

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r7.speaker: النضر
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r7.claim: Al-Naḍr had claimed that al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā would intercede for him; the verse was revealed in response.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r7.anchor: عن عكرمة قال قال النضر : سوف تشفع لي اللات والعزى . فنزلت : ولقد جئتموها فرادى

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r8.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r8.claim: Al-Suddī says polytheists worshipped idols believing they would intercede before God and were partners with Him; God is exalted above their claim.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1349/r8.anchor: عن السدى : قوله : وما نرى معكم شفعاءكم الذين زعمتم انهم فيكم شركاء قال : فان المشركين يزعمون

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1350/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1350/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1350/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets what was severed among them as kinship ties and the abode.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1350/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قوله : لقد تقطع بينكم وضل عنكم ما كنتم تزعمون يعني الارحام ، والمنزل

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1350/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1350/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1350/r2.claim: Mujāhid says the severed connection was their mutual ties in worldly life.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1350/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد : قوله : لقد تقطع بينكم ، والبين : تواصلهم في الدنيا

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1350/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1350/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1350/r3.claim: Al-Suddī explains that whatever had been between them was cut off.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1350/r3.anchor: عن السدى : قوله : لقد تقطع بينكم يقول : تقطع ما كان بينكم

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1350/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1350/r4.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1350/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the severed bond was what had been between the people and their gods.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1350/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك : لقد تقطع بينكم يعني ما كان بينهم وبين الهتهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r1.claim: If the omitted speaker of أخرجوا أنفسكم is God, this clause is coordinated with that command and belongs to the same implied speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r1.anchor: كان قوله { ولقد جئتمونا فرادى } عطفا على جملة { أخرجوا أنفسكم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r2.claim: If the death scene in 6:93 is literal, the past verb expresses the near future, like the call قد قامت الصلاة, as they approach God's sole control.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r2.anchor: في حين النزع يكون فعل { جئتمونا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r3.claim: If the implied speaker is the angels, the clause instead coordinates with 6:93's opening scene, shifting from observers addressed about wrongdoers to the wrongdoers directly.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r3.anchor: عطف على جملة : { ولو ترى إذ الظالمون }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r4.claim: Under the first construction, the past is literal because they have already come before God when told this; قد confirms the completed arrival.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r4.anchor: فعلى الوجه الأول يكون { جئتمونا } حقيقة في الماضي لأنهم حينما يقال لهم هذا القول قد حصل منهم المجيء بين يدي الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r5.claim: Under the second construction, past tense refers to the future to assert its certainty, with قد reinforcing the figurative usage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r5.anchor: يكون الماضي معبرا به عن المستقبل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r6.claim: The statement is not new information; it rebukes them by establishing the truth of the resurrection and judgment before God that they denied.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r6.anchor: وتوقيفهم على صدق ما كانوا ينذرون به على لسان الرسول فينكرونه وهو الرجوع إلى الحياة بعد الموت للحساب بين يدي الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r7.claim: The phrase may also evoke their arriving at a state they thought impossible, as in 24:39; the rajiz's line illustrates this sense of becoming.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r7.anchor: وقد يقصد مع هذا المعنى معنى الحصول في المكنة والمصير إلى ما كانوا يحسبون أنهم لا يصيرون إليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r8.speaker: الراجز
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r8.claim: The rajiz's line قد يصبح الله إمام الساري is cited as evidence for the sense of coming to be or attaining a state.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r9.claim: The attached نا refers to God rather than the angels, as shown by the following comparison to God's creating them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p381/r9.anchor: ضمير الجلالة وليس ضمير الملائكة بدليل قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r1.claim: فرادى is a circumstantial accusative describing the subject of جئتمونا: they arrive detached from the wealth, children, and supporters they once boasted of.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r1.anchor: و { فرادى } حال من الضمير المرفوع في { جئتمونا } أي منعزلين عن كل ما كنتم تعتزون به في الحياة الأولى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r2.claim: The stronger analysis treats فرادى as the broken plural of فردان, like سكارى from سكران, meaning solitary individuals.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r2.anchor: والأظهر أن ( فرادى ) جمع فردان مثل سكارى لسكران

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r3.claim: This form is not the same as the indeclinable distributive فراد, meaning one by one; here each arrives separately from his property.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r3.anchor: فراد المعدول يدل على معنى فردا فردا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r4.claim: The comparison means they are revived after death, which they denied, just as they directly witnessed their first creation; compare 50:15.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r4.anchor: تشبيه للمجيء أريد منه معنى الإحياء بعد الموت الذي كانوا ينكرونه فقد رأوه رأي العين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r5.claim: The كاف compares the new creation with the first creation and functions as an absolute object; ما after it is a verbal noun.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r5.anchor: فالكاف لتشبيه الخلق الجديد بالخلق الأول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r6.claim: تخويل means bestowing a favor or gift.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r7.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r7.claim: An etymology says تخويل originally meant giving servants, then broadened metaphorically to grants that benefit people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r7.anchor: أصله إعطاء الخول بفتحتين وهو الخدم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r8.claim: The word broadened metaphorically to all beneficial gifts, such as wealth and other blessings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r8.anchor: استعمل مجازا في إعطاء مطلق ما ينفع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r9.claim: ما is a relative pronoun here.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r9.anchor: و ( ما ) موصولة ومعنى تركهم إياه وراء ظهورهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r10.claim: Leaving gifts behind the back pictures the one who departs from a thing and leaves it behind; what someone prepares for himself is instead said to be before him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p382/r10.anchor: حال البعيد عن الشيء بمن بارحه سائرا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383/r1.claim: وتركتم is coordinated with جئتمونا and further explains فرادى by specifying how they are alone: they left worldly life behind.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383/r1.anchor: { وتركتم } عطف على { جئتمونا } وهو يبين معنى { فرادى } إلا أن في الجملة الثانية زيادة بيان لمعنى الانفراد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383/r2.claim: Both statements rebuke them for denying that they would come to judgment and for living as though they would remain in the world forever.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383/r2.anchor: لأن كلا الخبرين مستعمل في التخطئة والتنديم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqa instead parses the clause as a circumstantial state of the subject in جئتمونا, making their abandonment of gifts the point of censure.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383/r3.anchor: وأبو البقاء جعل الجملة حالا من الواو في { جئتمونا } فيصير ترك ما خولوه هو محل التنكيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383/r4.claim: The statement about seeing no intercessors is likewise coordinated with the preceding clauses and serves the same rebuking, regret-inducing purpose.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383/r4.anchor: وكذلك القول في جملة { وما نرى معكم شفعاءكم } أنها معطوفة على { جئتمونا وتركتم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383/r5.claim: When anxious about Islam, polytheists consoled themselves that their gods would intercede for them before God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383/r5.anchor: فالمشركون كانوا إذا اضطربت قلوبهم في أمر الإسلام عللوا أنفسهم بأن آلهتهم تشفع لهم عند الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383/r6.speaker: النضر بن الحارث
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383/r6.claim: A report says al-Nadr ibn al-Harith claimed that their gods would intercede; Ibn Ashur allows that he may have said it mockingly or from ignorance, but says the passage is not a discrete occasion of revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383/r6.anchor: أن النضر بن الحارث قال ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383#2/r1.claim: The denial taunts them as if the speaker were looking for expected intercessors: negating a description can suggest that its subject exists, and the present tense feigns that they may yet appear.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383#2/r1.anchor: تهكم بهم لأنهم لا شفعاء لهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383#2/r2.claim: Their supposed intercessors are the idols they worshipped, claiming they would bring them near to God and intercede for them.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383#2/r3.claim: زعم is false assertion, whether intentional deceit as in 4:60 or mistaken belief as here and in 6:22.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383#2/r3.anchor: والزعم : القول الباطل سواء كان عن تعمد للباطل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383#2/r4.claim: Fronting فيكم focuses attention on the astonishing claim that idols share in the human beings God created and alone deserves worship from.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p383#2/r4.anchor: وتقديم المجرور في قوله : { فيكم شركاء }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r1.claim: Ibn Ashur had explained intercession at 2:48.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r1.anchor: وتقدم معنى الشفاعة عند قوله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r2.claim: This explanatory resumption answers the hope prompted by the taunt: after pretending to leave open a chance of meeting their intercessors, it tells them in despair that their connection is severed.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r3.claim: The pronoun in بينكم includes both the addressed idolaters and their supposed intercessors.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r3.anchor: والضمير المضاف إليه عائد إلى المخاطبين وشفعائهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r4.speaker: نافع والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r4.claim: Nafi, al-Kisai, and Hafs read the ن with fatḥa, preserving بين as a locative adverb for the place of connection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r4.anchor: وقرأ نافع ، والكسائي ، وحفص عن عاصم بفتح نون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r5.speaker: البقية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r5.claim: The other readers pronounce the ن with ḍamma, turning بين from an adverb into a declinable noun to which severance is ascribed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r5.anchor: وقرأ البقية بضم نون { بينكم } على إخراج ( بين ) عن الظرفية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r6.claim: With fatḥa, بين is adverbial and the subject of تقطع is omitted; it is an indefinite connection, such as a rope, that was severed.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r7.claim: The concise construction has become proverbial; Arabs commonly use severing as a metaphor for distance and the collapse of connection, borrowing the rope image.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r7.anchor: وقد شاع في كلام العرب ذكر التقطع مستعارا للبعد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r8.speaker: امرؤ القيس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r8.claim: Imru al-Qays's verse uses severing to mean the breaking of the bonds of desire and passion, witnessing the metaphor for a lost connection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r8.anchor: قال امرؤ القيس : تقطع أسباب اللبانة والهوى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari proposes making the verbal noun derived from تقطع its grammatical subject.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r9.anchor: وقدر الزمخشري المصدر المأخوذ من { تقطع } فاعلا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r10.speaker: التفتزاني
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r10.claim: Al-Taftazani prefers an implicit الأمر as subject, understood as the matter between them having been severed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r10.anchor: وقال التفتزاني : ( الأولى أنه أسند إلى ضمير الأمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r11.claim: Another proposal makes بينكم an adjective standing for an omitted noun such as أمر بينكم; Ibn Ashur rejects this as an unattested analysis with no antecedent for a hidden pronoun.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p385/r11.anchor: صفة أقيمت مقام الموصوف الذي هو المسند إليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386/r1.claim: On the nominative reading, بينكم is the subject: it is a noun for the place where the group meets, figuratively signifying the separation of those who once met there.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386/r1.anchor: على قراءة الرفع جعل { بينكم } فاعلا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386/r2.claim: وَضل is coordinated with تقطع and continues the taunt and their loss of hope.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386/r2.anchor: عطف على { تقطع بينكم } وهو من تمام التهكم والتأييس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386/r3.claim: ضل means failed to find the way: the idols do not know where their worshippers are and cannot find them to intercede.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386/r3.anchor: أي جهل شفعاؤكم مكانكم لما تقطع بينكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386/r4.claim: ما is a relative pronoun referring to the idols; the parallel clause makes the two omitted objects of زعم recoverable, and ما suits their uselessness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386/r4.anchor: و ( ما ) موصولة ماصدقها الشفعاء لاتحاد صلتها وصلة { الذين زعمتم أنهم فيكم شركاء }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386/r5.speaker: ابن عطية وغيره
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386/r5.claim: Ibn Atiyya and others instead take ضل to mean disappeared or perished and ما as a verbal noun: the claim that the idols intercede has vanished; Ibn Ashur says his account is more forceful.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386/r5.anchor: وفسر ابن عطية وغيره ضل بمعنى غاب وتلف وذهب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386/r6.claim: Ibn Ashur rejects the alternative verbal-noun reading in favor of the sharper image of idols unable to find their worshippers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p386/r6.anchor: وما ذكرناه في تفسير الآية أبلغ وأوقع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r1.claim: Speech to people after their souls are taken, either as they leave their bodies or on Resurrection Day; both are possible.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r1.anchor: هذه حكاية عما يقال لهم بعد قبض أرواحهم، فإما عند خروجها من الأجساد وإما يوم القيامة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r2.claim: فرادى means one by one; its final alif is the feminine alif.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r2.anchor: فرادى معناه فردا فردا، والألف في آخره ألف تأنيث

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r3.speaker: ابن مقبل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r3.claim: Ibn Muqbil's verse uses فرادى alongside مثنى.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r3.anchor: ومنه قول الشاعر [ابن مقبل] : ترى النعرات الزرق تحت لبانه ... فرادى ومثنى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r4.speaker: أبو حيوة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r4.claim: Abu Haywa reads it with tanwin on the فعال pattern, a Tamim dialect.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة «فرادى» منونا على وزن فعال وهي لغة تميم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r5.claim: It is also explained as plural of فرد with open or quiescent ra.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r5.anchor: فرادى قيل هو جمع فرد بفتح الراء، وقيل جمع فرد بإسكان الراء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r6.claim: The verse confronts unbelievers with their solitude, lack of helpers, loss of worldly gifts and intercessors, and need for God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r6.anchor: والمقصد في الآية توقيف الكفار على انفرادهم وقلة النصير واحتياجهم إلى الله عز وجل بفقد الخول والشفعاء،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r7.claim: One explanation compares their solitude to their isolation at first creation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r7.anchor: فيكون قوله: كما خلقناكم أول مرة تشبيها بالانفراد الأول في وقت الخلقة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r8.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r8.claim: The comparison may also include the Prophet's description that people are resurrected barefoot, naked, uncircumcised.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r8.anchor: والإشارة على هذا بقوله كما هي إلى ما قاله النبي عليه السلام في صفة من يحشر أنهم يحشرون حفاة عراة غرلا،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r10.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r10.claim: Abu Amr ibn al-Ala recites Zuhayr's verse as evidence for the use of يستخولوا and يخولوا.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r10.anchor: وكان أبو عمرو بن العلاء ينشد بيت زهير: [الطويل] : هنالك إن يستخولوا المال يخولوا ... وإن يسألوا يعطوا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r11.claim: “Behind your backs” points to the worldly life, where they leave possessions behind.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r11.anchor: وراء ظهوركم إشارة إلى الدنيا لأنهم يتركون ذلك موجودا.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r12.claim: The challenge exposes the error of worshipping and venerating idols.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r12.anchor: وقوله تعالى: وما نرى معكم شفعاءكم الآية، توقيف على الخطأ في عبادة الأصنام وتعظيمها،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r13.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r13.claim: Al-Tabari transmits a report that it was revealed about al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, who expected al-Lat and al-Uzza to intercede; no grade is stated.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r13.anchor: قال الطبري: وروي أن هذه الآية نزلت في النضر بن الحارث لأنه قال سوف تشفع له اللات والعزى.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r14.claim: It addresses most Arabs, who thought idols interceded and brought them near God; those who recognized no other deity are outside its address.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r14.anchor: ومن كان من العرب يعتقد أنها تشفع وتقرب إلى الله زلفى ويرى شركتها بهذا الوجه فمخاطبته بالآية متمكن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r15.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة ونافع والكساء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r15.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Asim, Ibn Amir, and Hamza read nominative; Nafi and al-Kisa read accusative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r15.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر، وحمزة «بينكم» بالرفع، وقرأ نافع والكساء «بينكم» بالنصب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r16.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r16.claim: One nominative analysis uses بين as a noun and subject; Abu Ali al-Farisi favors it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r16.anchor: أولاها أنه الظرف استعمل اسما وأسند إليه الفعل كما قد استعملوه، اسما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r17.speaker: الزهراوي والمهدوي وأبو الفتح
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r17.claim: Al-Zahrawi, al-Mahdawi, Abu al-Fath, and others say البين can mean separation or connection, giving “your bond has been severed.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324/r17.anchor: الزهراوي والمهدوي وأبو الفتح وسواهم حكوا أن «البين» في اللغة يقال على الافتراق وعلى الوصل فكأنه قال لقد تقطع وصلكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya objects that “connection” is not attested orally from Arabs and may have been inferred from this verse, which allows other readings.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r1.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وفي هذا عندي اعتراض لأن ذلك لم يرو مسموعا عن العرب وإنما انتزع من الآية،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r2.speaker: الخليل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r2.claim: Al-Khalil's al-Ayn gives البين the sense “connection.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r2.anchor: قال الخليل في العين «والبين» الوصل. لقوله عز وجل: لقد تقطع بينكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r3.speaker: أبو الفتح
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r3.claim: Abu al-Fath supports the connection sense with a later poet's wordplay.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r3.anchor: أما إن أبا الفتح قوى أن «البين» الوصل وقال: «وقد أتقن ذلك بعض المحدثين بقوله: قد أنصف البين من البين» .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r4.claim: A further nominative analysis keeps البين in its basic sense of separation and uses تقطع figuratively for great distance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r4.anchor: والوجه الثالث من وجوه الرفع أن يكون «البين» على أصله في الفرقة من بان يبين إذا بعد،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r5.claim: For the accusative reading, an omitted subject such as connection is severed; Ibn Atiyya calls this clear.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r5.anchor: وأما وجه قراءة النصب فأن يكون ظرفا ويكون الفعل مستندا إلى شيء محذوف وتقديره لقد تقطع الاتصال أو الارتباط بينكم أو نحو هذا.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد والسدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r6.claim: Mujahid and al-Suddi explain the accusative reading with an omitted connection as what is severed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r6.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد رضي الله عنه: وهذا وجه واضح وعليه فسره الناس: مجاهد والسدي وغيرهما،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r7.speaker: أبو الحسن الأخفش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r7.claim: Al-Akhfash says the verb is predicated on the accusative adverb, understood as nominative, as in 72:11.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r7.anchor: وجه آخر يراه أبو الحسن الأخفش وهو أن يكون الفعل مسندا إلى الظرف ويبقى الظرف على حال نصبه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود ومجاهد والأعمش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r8.claim: Ibn Masud, Mujahid, and al-Amash read تقطع ما بينكم, adding ما.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود ومجاهد والأعمش «تقطع ما بينكم» بزيادة ما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r9.claim: ضل means vanished and went away.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r10.claim: Their claims were that idols interceded and shared in divinity.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p324#2/r10.anchor: وما كنتم تزعمون يريد دعواهم أنها تشفع وتشارك الله في الألوهية.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r1.speaker: عكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r1.claim: Ikrima says the verse was revealed after al-Nadr ibn al-Harith claimed al-Lat and al-Uzza would intercede for him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r1.anchor: سبب نزولها أن النضر بن الحارث قال سوف تشفع لي اللات والعزى فنزلت هذه الآية قاله عكرمة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r2.claim: Furādā means coming alone; the verse describes God's rebuke of polytheists on Resurrection Day.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r2.anchor: ومعنى فرادى وحدانا وهذا إخبار من الله تعالى بما يوبخ به المشركين يوم القيامة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
