IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r3.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses furādā as each person coming singly.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r3.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة فرادى أي فرد فرد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r4.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r4.claim: Ibn Qutayba identifies furādā as the plural of fard.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r4.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة فرادى جمع فرد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says they come separated from their families, wealth, and children.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r5.anchor: أحدها فرادى من الأهل والمال والولد قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r6.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says each person comes apart from the others.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r6.anchor: والثاني كل واحد على حدة قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r7.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r7.claim: Muqatil says they come with nothing from worldly life.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r7.anchor: والثالث ليس معكم من الدنيا شيء قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r8.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj says each is separated from his partner in error and his full brother.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r8.anchor: والرابع كل واحد منفرد عن شريكه في الغي وشقيقه قاله الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r9.speaker: ابن كيسان
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r9.claim: Ibn Kaysan says they come separated from the beings they worshipped.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88/r9.anchor: والخامس فرادى من المعبودين قاله ابن كيسان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r1.claim: One explanation is that people return without wealth, family, or children.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r1.anchor: أحدها لا مال ولا أهل ولا ولد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r2.claim: Another explanation says they return barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised; ghurl means those with foreskins.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r2.anchor: والثاني حفاة عراة غرلا والغرل القلف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r3.claim: A third explanation is that they return alive, as they were first created.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r4.claim: Khawwalnākum means We granted you ownership.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r5.claim: Behind your backs means that you left these things behind in worldly life.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r5.anchor: أي في الدنيا والمعنى أن ما دأبتم في تحصيله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r6.claim: What people spent their lives acquiring has vanished, leaving regret over their poor choices.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r6.anchor: والمعنى أن ما دأبتم في تحصيله في الدنيا فني وبقي الندم على سوء الاختيار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the claimed intercessors as idols or gods believed to intercede for their worshippers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r7.anchor: أحدهما أنها الأصنام قال ابن عباس شفعاؤكم أي آلهتكم الذين زعمتم أنهم يشفعون لكم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r8.claim: The phrase means that, in the idolaters' own view, their gods were partners.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r8.anchor: أي عندكم شركاء وقال ابن قتيبة زعمتم أنهم لي في خلقكم شركاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r9.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r9.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains the claim as making idols God's partners in creating them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r9.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة زعمتم أنهم لي في خلقكم شركاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r10.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r10.claim: The other view identifies the intercessors as angels, whom the polytheists believed would intercede.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r10.anchor: والثاني أنها الملائكة كانوا يعتقدون شفاعتها قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r11.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة وأبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r11.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, Hamza, and Abu Bakr from Asim read the final word in the nominative.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r11.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة وأبو بكر عن عاصم بالرفع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r12.speaker: الكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r12.claim: Al-Kisa'i and Hafs from Asim read it with the nūn in the accusative as an adverbial construction.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r12.anchor: والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم بنصب النون على الظرف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r13.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r13.claim: Al-Zajjaj prefers the nominative: the bond between the people has been severed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r13.anchor: قال الزجاج الرفع أجود ومعناه لقد تقطع وصلكم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r14.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r14.claim: The accusative is also possible, meaning that what was between them has been cut off.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r14.anchor: والنصب جائز ومعناه لقد تقطع ما كنتم فيه من الشركة بينكم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r15.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r15.claim: Ibn al-Anbari supplies an omitted phrase: what was between you was severed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r15.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري التقدير لقد تقطع ما بينكم فحذف ما لوضوح معناها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r16.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r16.speaker: أبو علي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r16.claim: Abu Ali says nominative readers make the word the subject of the verb, meaning their bond was severed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r16.anchor: قال أبو علي الذين رفعوه جعلوه اسما فأسندوا الفعل الذي هو تقطع إليه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r17.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r17.speaker: أبو علي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r17.claim: Abu Ali says accusative readers infer a subject within the verb, namely the bond.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r17.anchor: والذين نصبوا أضمروا اسم الفاعل في الفعل والمضمر هو الوصل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r18.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r18.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r18.claim: One explanation of what they used to claim is the intercession of their gods.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r18.anchor: وفي الذي كانوا يزعمون قولان أحدهما شفاعة آلهتهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r19.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r19.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p88#2/r19.claim: Another explanation of what they used to claim is that there would be no resurrection or requital.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p302/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p302/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p302/r1.claim: At Resurrection people are told they have come alone as they were first created; just as God began their creation, He brings them back, though they had denied and deemed this unlikely.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p302/r1.anchor: أي: يقال لهم يوم معادهم هذا، كما قال {وعرضوا على ربك صفا لقد جئتمونا كما خلقناكم أول مرة}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p302/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p302/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p302/r2.claim: What people leave behind is the worldly blessing and wealth they acquired.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p302/r2.anchor: أي: من النعم والأموال التي اقتنيتموها في الدار الدنيا {وراء ظهوركم}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p302/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p302/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p302/r3.claim: In an authentic report, the Prophet says a person’s wealth is only what was eaten and consumed, worn out, or given in charity and sent ahead; everything else is left to others.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p302/r3.anchor: وثبت في الصحيح أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "يقول ابن آدم: مالي مالي، وهل لك من مالك إلا ما أكلت فأفنيت،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p302/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p302/r4.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p302/r4.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri says the son of Adam will be brought like a young goat and asked where his amassed wealth is; when he says he left it full, God asks what he sent ahead for himself, and he will have sent nothing, so al-Hasan recites this verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p302/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري: يؤتى بابن آدم يوم القيامة كأنه بذج فيقول الله، عز وجل، [له] (1) أين ما جمعت؟ فيقول يا رب،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p303/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p303/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p303/r1.claim: The verse rebukes idolaters for taking rivals and idols, assuming they would benefit them in worldly life and the afterlife, if there is an afterlife; at Resurrection those ties and delusions collapse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p303/r1.anchor: تقريع لهم وتوبيخ على ما كانوا اتخذوا في [الدار] (2) الدنيا من الأنداد والأصنام والأوثان، ظانين أن تلك تنفعهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p303/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p303/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p303/r2.claim: The alleged partners had a share, in the idolaters' view, in deserving their worship.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p303/r2.anchor: أي: في العبادة، لهم فيكم قسط في استحقاق العبادة لهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p303/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p303/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p303/r3.claim: The nominative reading is explained as encompassing them; the accusative reading means the bonds and means between them have been severed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p303/r3.anchor: قرئ بالرفع، أي شملكم، وقرئ بالنصب، أي: لقد انقطع ما بينكم (6) من الوصلات والأسباب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p303/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p303/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p303/r4.claim: The vanished hopes in idols recur in passages where idolaters, their followers, and their supposed allies separate, fail to answer, and cannot rescue one another.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p303/r4.anchor: كما قال: {إذ تبرأ الذين اتبعوا من الذين اتبعوا ورأوا العذاب وتقطعت بهم الأسباب

JISHUMI:v3p2327/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2327/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2327/r6.claim: Abu Jaʿfar, Nafiʿ, Hafs from ʿAsim, and al-Kisaʾi read بينكم in the accusative; Hasan, Mujahid, Ibn Masʿud, and Abu Musa also transmit this reading, while the other readers use the nominative.
JISHUMI:v3p2327/r6.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وحفص عن عاصم والكسائي: بينكم نصبا، وهو قراءة الحسن ومجاهد

JISHUMI:v3p2327/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2327/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2327/r7.claim: With nominative بين, the meaning is that the ties you maintained in worldly life are severed; بين can mean either connection or separation, and here it is a noun, not an adverb.
JISHUMI:v3p2327/r7.anchor: فأما الرفع فعلى معنى تقطع وصلكم الذي كنتم تواصلون بها في الدنيا، والبين: الوصل، والبين: القطيعة

JISHUMI:v3p2327/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2327/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2327/r8.claim: With accusative بين, an implied ما gives the sense 'what was between you was severed'; the phrase refers to the partnership and بين is an adverb.
JISHUMI:v3p2327/r8.anchor: على إضمار (ما)، أي: تقطع ما بينكم

JISHUMI:v3p2327/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2327/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2327/r9.claim: فرادى means individually or alone; it is pluralized from فريد or فرد, like أسير/أسارى and وحد/آحاد, as al-Farra notes.
JISHUMI:v3p2327/r9.anchor: الفرادى: الوحدان، وهم المنفردون، واحده: فريد، وفعيل يجمع على فعالى كأسير وأسارى

JISHUMI:v3p2327/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2327/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2327/r10.claim: To give someone خول is to make him an owner of dependents, like giving him wealth or authority; خوله الله means He granted him something, and خولي مال means a steward of property.
JISHUMI:v3p2327/r10.anchor: والتخويل: تمليك الخول، كما أن التمويل تمليك الأموال. والتسويد تمليك السؤدد، وخوله الله: أعطاه

JISHUMI:v3p2327/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2327/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2327/r11.claim: A hadith says the Prophet would يتخول people with admonition, meaning he attended to them regularly; Abu ʿAmr corrects this to يتحولهم, choosing times when they were receptive.
JISHUMI:v3p2327/r11.anchor: وفي الحديث: كان يتخولهم بالموعظة أي: يتعهدهم، وقال أبو عمرو: الصواب يتحولهم بالحاء

JISHUMI:v3p2327/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2327/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2327/r12.claim: The phrase خول so-and-so can mean his followers; خائل is singular, and a gift given without recompense is also described as granting خول.
JISHUMI:v3p2327/r12.anchor: ويقال: هم خول فلان أي: أتباعه، الواحد: خائل، وكل من أعطى عطاء على غير جزاء فقد خوله

JISHUMI:v1p773/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p773/r1.speaker: إبراهيم بن أدهم
JISHUMI:v1p773/r1.claim: Asked why their supplications go unanswered, Ibrahim ibn Adham says they know God but disobey Him, know the Messenger but do not follow his Sunna, and know the Qur'an but do not act on it; they consume blessings without thanks, neglect Paradise and fear of Hell, fail to oppose Satan or prepare for death, bury the dead without reflection, and busy themselves with others' faults.
JISHUMI:v1p773/r1.anchor: فقال: لأنكم عرفتم الله فلم تطيعوه، وعرفتم الرسول - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فلم تتبعوا سنته،

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r1.claim: Furādā means individually or singly; it may imply arriving without helpers or without property.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r1.anchor: الفرادى الواحدان , ويحتمل وجهين : أحدهما : فرادى من الأعوان . والثاني : فرادى من الأموال .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r2.claim: What God granted and people left behind means their property; tawkhīl means granting ownership, as illustrated by Abu al-Najm's use of khawwala in poetry.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r2.anchor: يعني ما ملكناكم من الأموال , والتخويل تمليك المال

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r3.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi says the absent intercessors are the idols the people worshipped.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r3.anchor: فيه وجهان : أحدهما : آلهتهم التي كانوا يعبدونها , قاله الكلبي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r4.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r4.claim: Muqatil identifies the intercessors as angels whose intercession the people expected.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r4.anchor: والثاني : الملائكة الذين كانوا يعتقدون شفاعتهم , قاله مقاتل .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r5.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r5.claim: One explanation takes “partners among you” to mean intercessors, according to al-Kalbi.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r5.anchor: فيه وجهان : أحدهما : يعني شفعاء , قاله الكلبي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r6.claim: Alternatively, they thought alleged partners would bear their burdens for them, as partners might shoulder one another's loads.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r6.anchor: والثاني : أي متحملين عنكم تحمل الشركاء عن الشركاء .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r7.claim: The phrase may mean the gathering has broken apart in the afterlife, or that their bond has disappeared in this world, according to Mujahid.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r7.anchor: فيه وجهان : أحدهما : تفرق جمعكم في الآخرة . والثاني : ذهب تواصلكم في الدنيا , قاله مجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r8.claim: With fatḥa on bayn, the phrase means that the matter between them has been severed or decided.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r8.anchor: ومن قرأ { بينكم } بالفتح , فمعناه تقطع الأمر بينكم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r9.claim: What they claimed has vanished may be their denial of resurrection and recompense, or the intercessors they expected.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r9.anchor: فيه وجهان : أحدهما : من عدم البعث والجزاء . والثاني : من شفعائكم عند الله .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r10.claim: Although the verse uses past tense for a future scene, one answer is that it will be spoken to them in the afterlife, making it literally past from that perspective.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r10.anchor: أحدهما : أنه يقال لهم ذلك في الآخرة فهو على الظاهر إخبار .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r11.claim: The past tense can describe a future event because its certainty makes it as though it had happened already.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p145/r11.anchor: والثاني : أنه لتحققه بمنزلة ما كان , فجاز , وإن كان مستقبلا أن يعبر عنه بالماضي .

MUQATIL:6:94/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:94/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:94/r1.claim: At the Resurrection people come individually, bringing nothing from worldly life, just as they were born with nothing at their first creation.
MUQATIL:6:94/r1.anchor: { فرادى } ، ليس معكم من الدنيا شىء، { كما خلقناكم أول مرة } حين ولدوا وليس لهم شيء

MUQATIL:6:94/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:94/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:94/r2.claim: They leave behind in the world the good things God granted them after their own death.
MUQATIL:6:94/r2.anchor: يعنى ما أعطيناكم من الخير من بعدكم فى الدنيا

MUQATIL:6:94/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:94/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:94/r3.claim: The supposed intercessors are angels whom the idolaters claimed were partners and intercessors for them with God.
MUQATIL:6:94/r3.anchor: { وما نرى معكم شفعآءكم } من الملائكة، { الذين زعمتم } في الدنيا

MUQATIL:6:94/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:94/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:94/r4.claim: He connects their claim about intercessors to 10:18, where they say, These are our intercessors with God.

MUQATIL:6:94/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:94/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:94/r5.claim: The bond of affection and contact between the idolaters and their angelic partners is severed; their claim that God has a partner has vanished.
MUQATIL:6:94/r5.anchor: يعنى من الملائكة من المودة والتواصل، { وضل عنكم } فى الآخرة { ما كنتم تزعمون }

NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r1.claim: They come before God for judgment and recompense.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r2.claim: They arrive alone, without property or helper; furādā is a plural like asīr/asārā.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r2.anchor: منفردين بلا مال ولا معين هو جمع فريد كاسير وأسارى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r3.claim: «As We created you» describes their coming in the accusative: they come as they were first created.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r3.anchor: فى محل النصب صفة لمصدر جئتمونا أى مجيئا مثل ما خلقناكم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r4.claim: They return alone in the form in which they were born.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r4.anchor: على الهيآت التى ولدتم عليها فى الانفراد

NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r5.claim: What God bestowed is what He had given them as property; they leave it behind and carry away not even a tiny amount.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r5.anchor: ﴿ وراء ظهوركم ﴾ ولم تحتملوا منه نقيرا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r6.claim: They do not see the intercessors they claimed were partners in their worship.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r7.speaker: الزجاج
NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj says bayn means connection, though the word also means separation or estrangement; cited poetry evokes longing for separation.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r7.anchor: عن الزجاج والبين الوصل والهجر قال فوالله لولا البين لم يكن الهوى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r8.speaker: مدنى وعلى وحفص
NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r8.claim: The Medinan reader, ʿAlī, and Ḥafṣ read «baynakum» with fatḥa, meaning that severing occurred among them.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r8.anchor: بينكم مدنى وعلى وحفص أى وقع التقطع بينكم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p335#2/r9.claim: What they claimed disappeared, was wasted, and proved false.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r1.claim: The verse depicts resurrection; furada is accusative circumstantial and indeclinable because it ends in the feminine alif.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r1.anchor: هذه عبارة عن الحشر. و«فرادى» في موضع نصب على الحال، ولم ينصرف لأن فيه ألف تأنيث.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r2.speaker: أبو حيوة
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r2.claim: Abu Haywa reads furada with tanwin; it is Tamim's dialect, which does not use that form in the nominative.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة «فرادا» بالتنوين وهي لغة تميم، ولا يقولون في موضع الرفع فراد.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r3.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r3.claim: Ahmad b. Yahya records furad without tanwin and compares it with thulath and rubaa.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r3.anchor: وحكى أحمد بن يحيى «فراد» بلا تنوين، قال: مثل ثلاث ورباع

QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r4.claim: Furada is plural of fardan, like sukara from sakran and kusala from kaslan; other singular forms include fard and farid.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r4.anchor: و«فرادى» جمع فردان كسكارى جمع سكران، وكسالى جمع كسلان.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r5.speaker: الأعرج
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r5.claim: Al-A'raj reads farda without the alif, on the pattern of sukra and kusla.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r5.anchor: وقرأ الأعرج «فردى» مثل سكرى وكسلى بغير ألف.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r6.claim: People come one by one, alone without family, wealth, children, or worldly allies; what they worshipped besides God will not benefit them.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r6.anchor: والمعنى: جئتمونا واحدا واحدا، كل واحد منكم منفردا بلا أهل ولا مال ولا ولد ولا ناصر

QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r7.claim: One explanation says they come as first created: naked, barefoot, uncircumcised, and without possessions, as when born.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r7.anchor: وقيل: عراة كما خرجتم من بطون أمهاتكم حفاة غرلا بهما ليس معهم شيء.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r8.speaker: العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r8.claim: Scholars say people are resurrected with the limbs they had at birth; removed limbs are restored, including what circumcision removed, explaining ghurla.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r8.anchor: وقال العلماء: يحشر العبد غدا وله من الأعضاء ما كان له يوم ولد فمن قطع منه عضو يرد في القيامة عليه.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r9.claim: Khawwalnakum means 'We gave you and made you owners'; al-khawl includes God's gifts of servants and livestock.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r9.anchor: أي أعطيناكم وملكناكم. والخول: ما أعطاه الله للإنسان من العبيد والنعم.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r11.claim: The alleged intercessors are idols worshipped and made God's partners; polytheists claimed idols were God's partners and intercessors.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r11.anchor: أي الذين عبدتموهم وجعلتموهم شركاء يريد الأصنام أي شركائي. وكان المشركون يقولون

QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r12.claim: Nafi, al-Kisai, and Hafs read baynakum accusative as an adverb with an understood connection; the partners' disavowal severs the relationship.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r12.anchor: قرأ نافع والكسائي وحفص بالنصب على الظرف، على معنى لقد تقطع وصلكم بينكم.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r13.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r13.claim: Ibn Masud's codex reads 'what was between you has been severed'; because 'what' names the severed thing, the syntax requires the accusative.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r13.anchor: وفي حرف ابن مسعود ما يدل على النصب فيه «لقد تقطع ما بينكم». وهذا لا يجوز فيه إلا النصب

QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r14.claim: Another explanation says the matter between them has been cut off; this is close in meaning to the severed-connection interpretation.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r14.anchor: وقيل: المعنى لقد تقطع الأمر بينكم. والمعنى متقارب.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r15.claim: Other readers use the nominative, treating bayn as noun and verb subject; examples where a preposition governs it support this analysis.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94/r15.anchor: وقرأ الباقون «بينكم» بالرفع على أنه اسم غير ظرف، فأسند الفعل إليه فرفع. ويقوي جعل «بين» اسما

QURTUBI-FULL:6:94#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94#2/r1.claim: The phrases 'a barrier between us and you' and 'this is the parting between me and you' support treating bayn as a noun.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:94#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94#2/r2.claim: Al-Qurtubi accepts the accusative reading as nominative in syntax and concludes the readings agree in meaning.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94#2/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون قراءة النصب على معنى الرفع، وإنما نصب لكثرة استعماله ظرفا منصوبا وهو في موضع رفع، وهو مذهب الأخفش فالقراءتان على هذا بمعنى واحد، فاقرأ بأيهما شئت.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:94#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94#2/r3.claim: Dalla ankum means 'went away'; their claims were false assertions in worldly life.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94#2/r3.anchor: { وضل عنكم } أي ذهب. { ما كنتم تزعمون } أي تكذبون به في الدنيا

QURTUBI-FULL:6:94#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94#2/r4.claim: A report says the verse was revealed concerning al-Nadr b. al-Harith.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94#2/r4.anchor: روي أن الآية نزلت في النضر بن الحارث.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:94#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94#2/r5.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94#2/r5.claim: Aisha feared men and women would be resurrected together and see one another naked; the Prophet replied each would be occupied and not look at the other sex.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94#2/r5.anchor: أن عائشة رضي الله عنها قرأت قول الله تعالى: «ولقد جئتمونا فرادى كما خلقناكم أول مرة» فقالت: يا رسول الله، واسوءتاه

QURTUBI-FULL:6:94#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94#2/r6.speaker: رسول الله
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94#2/r6.claim: The Prophet says each person will be occupied with his or her own affair, so men will not look at women nor women at men; al-Qurtubi calls it sound and says Muslim transmits it by meaning.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:94#2/r6.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لكل امرىء منهم يومئذ شأن يغنيه لا ينظر الرجال إلى النساء ولا النساء إلى الرجال شغل بعضهم عن بعض»

QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r6.claim: The return echoes 6:94, where people come singly as first created.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r6.anchor: ولقد جئتمونا فرادى كما خلقناكم أول مرة

BURSEVI:v3p53#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p53#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p53#2/r1.claim: Coming is for reckoning and recompense; the past form depicts a certain future, as in 16:1.

BURSEVI:v3p53#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p53#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p53#2/r2.claim: The address is to Quraysh, revealed after they boasted of wealth and children and mocked the poor, claiming they would not be punished in the afterlife.
BURSEVI:v3p53#2/r2.anchor: والخطاب لكفار قريش لأنها نزلت حين قالوا افتخارا واستخفافا للفقراء

BURSEVI:v3p53#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p53#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p53#2/r3.claim: فرادى is plural of فرد: each person stands alone, separated from wealth, children, and worldly things they preferred.
BURSEVI:v3p53#2/r3.anchor: {فرادى} جمع فرد أي منفردين عن الأموال والأولاد

BURSEVI:v3p53#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p53#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p53#2/r4.claim: The comparison may be appositive to فرادى or a circumstantial phrase describing their solitude.
BURSEVI:v3p53#2/r4.anchor: بدل من فرادى أي على الهيئة التي ولدتم عليها في الانفراد

BURSEVI:v3p53#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p53#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p53#2/r5.claim: They are resurrected as first created: naked, barefoot, uncircumcised, and without conditions acquired in earthly life.
BURSEVI:v3p53#2/r5.anchor: مشبهين ابتداء خلقكم عراة حفاة غرلا بهما

BURSEVI:v3p53#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p53#2/r6.speaker: عائشة رضي الله عنها والرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v3p53#2/r6.claim: Aisha exclaimed at men and women being resurrected naked; the Prophet replied each would be too occupied to look at the other sex.
BURSEVI:v3p53#2/r6.anchor: قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها واسوءتاه الرجل والمرأة كذلك فقال عليه السلام : "لكل امرىء منهم يومئذ شأن يغنيه

BURSEVI:v3p53#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p53#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p53#2/r7.claim: What God bestowed was worldly property that distracted people from the afterlife.
BURSEVI:v3p53#2/r7.anchor: ما تفضلنا به عليكم في الدنيا فشغلتم به عن الآخرة

BURSEVI:v3p53#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p53#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p53#2/r8.claim: Takhwīl is either ownership of retainers and servants, or a gift granted without recompense.
BURSEVI:v3p53#2/r8.anchor: والتخويل تمليك الخول ، أي : الخدم والأتباع

BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r1.claim: They left behind what they had not sent ahead as good deeds; unlike believers, whose sound beliefs and righteous works accompany them to the gathering, so they are not truly alone.
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r1.anchor: ما قدمتم منه شيئا ولم تحملوا نقيرا بخلاف المؤمنين فإنهم صرفوا همتهم

BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r2.claim: The supposed intercessors are the idols.

BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r3.claim: They claimed the idols shared God's lordship over them and right to be worshiped.
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r3.anchor: شركاء الله في ربوبيتكم واستحقاق عبادتكم

BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r4.claim: The phrase means severance occurred between them, by analogy with the idiom that a joining was made between two things.
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r4.anchor: وقع التقطع بينكم كما يقال جمع بين الشيئين

BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r5.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r5.claim: Kashifi glosses this as the bond and affection between them having been severed.
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r5.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (منقطع كشت آنه ميان شما بود ازوصلت ومودت)

BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r6.claim: ضل عنكم means that what they relied on became void and was lost.

BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r7.claim: One reading is that they claimed their idols were intercessors, but the idols cannot avert punishment.
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r7.anchor: أنها شفعاؤكم فلم يقدروا على دفع شيء من العذاب عنكم

BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r8.claim: Alternatively they claimed the idols were partners in lordship; the author prefers this sense because it fits the preceding mention of alleged partners.
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r8.anchor: أو أنها شركاؤكمفي ربوبيتكم وهو الأنسب لسياق النظم

BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r9.claim: A person's four enemies are wealth, family, children, and friends; none enter the grave with the dead.
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r9.anchor: اعلم أن للإنسان أعداء أربعة هي : المال والأهل والأولاد والأصدقاء

BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r10.claim: The four companions entering the grave and interceding are the testimony of faith, prayer, fasting, and remembrance of God.
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r10.anchor: وأصدقاء أربعة هي : كلمة الشهادة والصلاة والصوم وذكر الله هي تدخل في القبر

BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r11.claim: The wise person prepares for solitude by acquiring taqwa as clothing and righteous action as a companion.
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r11.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن يتفكر في تجرده وتفرده فيسعى في تحصيل لباس له هو التقوى

BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r12.claim: A report says good deeds comfort, brighten, protect, and enlarge the grave; evil deeds frighten, darken, constrict, and torment their owner.
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r12.anchor: وفي الحديث : "إن عمل الإنسان يدفن معه في قبره

BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r13.speaker: اليافعي
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r13.claim: Al-Yafi‘i heard of a Yemeni righteous man who saw a black dog leave a grave after burial; the dog was the dead person's deeds, while Yasin and its companion sūras protected the deceased and drove it away.
BURSEVI:v3p53#3/r13.anchor: قال اليافعي : وقد سمعت عن بعض الصالحين في بعض بلاد اليمن

BURSEVI:v3p54/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p54/r1.speaker: السعدي
BURSEVI:v3p54/r1.claim: Sa‘di's verses teach worldly grief and joy pass, while deeds and a good name remain; possessions and status are no lasting support.
BURSEVI:v3p54/r1.anchor: غم وشادماني نماند وليك جزاى عمل ماندو نام نيك

BURSEVI:v3p54/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p54/r2.speaker: القشيري
BURSEVI:v3p54/r2.claim: Al-Qushayri says people enter and leave the world detached; ties and burdens accumulate, but wealth, status, and intercessors cannot rescue them at God's reckoning; their bonds, hopes, and efforts fail.
BURSEVI:v3p54/r2.anchor: قال القشيري : {ولقد جئتمونا فرادى} أي : دخلتم الدنيا بخرقة وخرجتم منها بخرقة

BURSEVI:v3p54/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p54/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p54/r3.claim: The journey to God proceeds through tajrīd, tafrīd, then tawḥīd. Tajrīd detaches from this world; tafrīd frees one from attachment to both worlds, as the spirit was before embodiment.
BURSEVI:v3p54/r3.anchor: والإشارة أن المجيء إلى الله يكون بالتجريد ثم بالتفريد ثم بالتوحيد

BURSEVI:v3p54/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p54/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p54/r4.claim: The first creation is the spirit before attachment to the body; he links this to embryonic creation in 23:14 and creation and forming in 7:11.
BURSEVI:v3p54/r4.anchor: كما كان في بدء الخلقة روحا مجردا عن تعلقات الكونين

BURSEVI:v3p54/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p54/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p54/r5.claim: The seeker strives to detach from both realms; worldly gifts signify their attachments. Supposed intercessors are deeds and states thought to lead to God, severed at journey's end.
BURSEVI:v3p54/r5.anchor: فللعبد في السير إلى الله كسب وسعي بالتجريد والتفريد عن الدنيا والآخرة

BURSEVI:v3p54/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p54/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p54/r6.claim: The journey ends at divine majesty, as Gabriel's ascent ended at the Lote Tree, the limit for angelic and human travelers. Tawḥīd receives divine oneness and joins the servant to unity.
BURSEVI:v3p54/r6.anchor: فإذا وصل العبد إلى سرادقات العزة انتهى سيره كما انتهى سير جبرائيل ليلة المعراج عند سدرة المنتهى

BURSEVI:v3p54/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p54/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p54/r7.claim: Without primordial divine care, the seeker would stop at the Lote Tree, saying each has a known station, as in 37:164.
BURSEVI:v3p54/r7.anchor: ولو لم تدركه العناية الأزلية بجذبات الربوبية لانقطع عن السير في الله بالله وبقي في السدرة

RAZI-FULL:v13p71/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p71/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p71/r1.claim: The opening is best read as continuing the angels’ rebuke in 6:93, with the whole speech reported by angels charged either with taking souls or with punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v13p71/r1.anchor: أن يكون هذا معطوفا على قول الملائكة { أخرجوا أنفسكم اليوم تجزون عذاب الهون بما كنتم تقولون } فبين تعالى أنهم كما يقولون ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v13p71/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p71/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p71/r2.claim: An alternative makes God the speaker; the issue is whether He speaks to disbelievers, since ‘He will not speak to them’ seems to deny it while 15:92 and 7:6 describe questioning. Rāzī prefers the angel-speech reading because of the conjunction.
RAZI-FULL:v13p71/r2.anchor: والقول الثاني : أن قائل هذا القول هو الله تعالى ومنشأ هذا الاختلاف إن الله تعالى هل يتكلم مع الكفار أو لا ؟

RAZI-FULL:v13p71/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p71/r3.speaker: ابن قتيبة
RAZI-FULL:v13p71/r3.claim: Ibn Qutaybah treats furādā as the plural of fardān, like sukkārā from sukkārān and kusālā from kaslān.
RAZI-FULL:v13p71/r3.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة : فرادى جمع فردان ، مثل سكارى وسكران

RAZI-FULL:v13p71/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p71/r4.speaker: غيره
RAZI-FULL:v13p71/r4.claim: Another grammarian takes furādā as plural of farīd, by analogy with ridāfā and radīf.
RAZI-FULL:v13p71/r4.anchor: وقال غيره فرادى : جمع فريد ، مثل ردافى ورديف

RAZI-FULL:v13p71/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p71/r5.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v13p71/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ lists four possible singular forms: fard, farda, farīd, and fardān.
RAZI-FULL:v13p71/r5.anchor: وقال الفراء : فرادى جمع واحده فرد وفردة وفريد وفردان

RAZI-FULL:v13p71/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p71/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p71/r6.claim: The rebuke recalls that people spent their effort gaining wealth and status and worshipping idols as intercessors; at resurrection the wealth is gone and idols cannot intercede, leaving them alone.
RAZI-FULL:v13p71/r6.anchor: المراد منه التقريع والتوبيخ ، وذلك لأنهم صرفوا جدهم وجهدهم في الدنيا إلى تحصيل أمرين

RAZI-FULL:v13p71/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p71/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p71/r7.claim: Believers spent life gaining true knowledge and righteous deeds; these remain with them in their graves and at resurrection, so they arrive with provisions for the afterlife rather than truly alone.
RAZI-FULL:v13p71/r7.anchor: بخلاف أهل الإيمان فإنهم صرفوا عمرهم إلى تحصيل المعارف الحقة

RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r1.speaker: نافع وحفص عن عاصم والكسائي
RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r1.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim, and al-Kisāʾī read baynakum in the accusative; it denotes the partnership or association that had joined them.
RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r1.anchor: قرأ نافع وحفص عن عاصم والكسائي { بينكم } بالنصب

RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r2.speaker: الباقون
RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r2.claim: The remaining readers use the nominative, construing bayn as the bond or connection that has been severed.
RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r2.anchor: والباقون بالرفع قال الزجاج : الرفع أجود ، ومعناه ، لقد تقطع وصلكم

RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r3.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj prefers the nominative reading, ‘your bond has been severed’; he accepts the accusative as meaning that the association between them has been severed.
RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج : الرفع أجود ، ومعناه ، لقد تقطع وصلكم

RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r4.speaker: أبو علي
RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r4.claim: Abū ʿAlī distinguishes a declinable noun like ‘separation’ from the preferable adverbial form, which can be reused as a noun; the cited usage in 41:5 and 18:78 supports this, while a maṣdar reading would distort the intended sense.
RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r4.anchor: قال أبو علي : هذا الاسم يستعمل على ضربين : أحدهما : أن يكون اسما منصرفا كالافتراق

RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r5.claim: Although the root suggests separation, bayn can denote a bond because it is used of two parties joined in some respect, such as partnership or kinship.
RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r5.anchor: هذا اللفظ إنما يستعمل في الشيئين اللذين بينهما مشاركة ومواصلة من بعض الوجوه ، كقولهم بيني وبينه شركة

RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r6.claim: For the accusative reading, the subject is understood: ‘your bond has been severed among you.’
RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r6.anchor: أما من قرأ { لقد تقطع بينكم } بالنصب فوجهه أنه أضمر الفاعل والتقدير : لقد تقطع وصلكم بينكم

RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r7.speaker: سيبويه
RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r7.claim: Sībawayh compares the ellipsis to ‘when it is tomorrow, come to me,’ where hope or misfortune is understood from context.
RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r7.anchor: وقال سيبويه : إنهم قالوا إذا كان غدا فأتني والتقدير : إذا كان الرجاء أو البلاء غدا فأتني

RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r8.speaker: ابن الأنباري
RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r8.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī supplies the omitted subject as mā baynakum, ‘what was between you,’ omitted because its meaning is clear.
RAZI-FULL:v13p72/r8.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري : التقدير : لقد تقطع ما بينكم

RAZI-FULL:v13p72#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p72#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p72#2/r1.claim: The body is an instrument for the soul to acquire true knowledge and virtue; dying without either leaves profound regret over wasting a means to eternal happiness.
RAZI-FULL:v13p72#2/r1.anchor: { ولقد جئتمونا فرادى كما خلقناكم أول مرة }

RAZI-FULL:v13p72#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p72#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p72#2/r2.claim: People invert their proper journey from bodily life toward the spiritual world by pursuing wealth and status; at death their possessions remain useless behind them, intensifying regret.
RAZI-FULL:v13p72#2/r2.anchor: والإنسان في الحقيقة متوجه من العالم الجسماني إلى العالم الروحاني

RAZI-FULL:v13p72#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p72#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p72#2/r3.claim: Wealth used for no good purpose is left behind, but wealth spent to honor God and show compassion to creation is sent ahead, as 2:110 says.
RAZI-FULL:v13p72#2/r3.anchor: كما قال تعالى : { وما تقدموا لانفسكم من خير تجدوه عند الله }

RAZI-FULL:v13p72#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p72#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p72#2/r4.claim: Those who labored for false religions expecting aid at the Resurrection instead encounter their doctrines’ severe, lasting punishment and the absence of their supposed partners.
RAZI-FULL:v13p72#2/r4.anchor: وما نرى معكم شفعاءكم الذين زعمتم أنهم فيكم شركاء

RAZI-FULL:v13p72#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p72#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p72#2/r5.claim: Their punishment includes regret for hardship spent gaining only torment, shame at recognizing their worldly beliefs as error, and despair after intense hope.
RAZI-FULL:v13p72#2/r5.anchor: منها عذاب الحسرة والندامة : وهو أنه كيف أنفق ماله

RAZI-FULL:v13p72#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p72#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p72#2/r6.claim: Once certainty makes recovery impossible, grief becomes acute; the severed connection between soul and body cannot be restored.
RAZI-FULL:v13p72#2/r6.anchor: والمعنى أن الوصلة الحاصلة بين النفس والجسد قد تقطعت ولا سبيل إلى تحصيلها مرة أخرى
